searchDocs.title: About Fegg​
searchDocs.content: Fegg is a small PHP framework, originally created by Genies, Inc. and extended by LionHeart with a CMS foundation (login, media and image management, post types).  LionHeart projects start from the skeleton repository lionheart-group/lh-fegg-skelton. It contains Fegg, the CMS, sample pages (top page, news, contact form) and the frontend build setup.

searchDocs.title: What is new in Fegg 5​
searchDocs.content: PHP 7.4 to 8.5 are supported.Core and site are separated. htdocs/_fegg/core/ is the core: the framework and the CMS foundation shared by every project. Do not edit it. fegg-cli core:update replaces it as a whole, the same way you update WordPress itself.htdocs/_fegg/site/ is the site: your project's controllers, templates and settings. Updates never touch it.To change something the core provides (a CMS template, a CMS screen, a setting), override it from site/. Namespaces and autoloading. Controllers are Site\Controller\... classes and framework classes are Fegg\... (Fegg\Model, Fegg\Validation, Fegg\Tool\Mail, ...). Create classes with new; getClass() is no longer needed.Errors fail loudly. Database errors throw Fegg\Database\QueryException and missing templates throw Fegg\Template\TemplateException. Uncaught, both become a logged HTTP 500 (the error page site/template/error/500.html can be your own) instead of a message printed into the page. Fegg\Log writes the application log.Per-server settings and secrets come from site/config/env.php (not committed) or environment variables, read with feggEnv(). FEGG_ENV (production unless set) decides whether developers see error details.Secure by default. Security headers on every response, sessions only when needed (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, strict mode), CSRF tokens in the CMS, login throttling, upload content checks.SQLite or MySQL. fegg-cli migration works on both.Command line tools. fegg-cli checks templates (template:lint), lists the database schema (db:schema), manages CMS users (user:create), updates the core (core:update) and checks that _fegg/ cannot be read from the web (doctor).  Fegg 4 code (MyApplication, getClass(), controllers without a namespace, Model, DB_pdo, LH_FW) still runs through a compatibility layer. Every use is logged as Fegg deprecated: ... in the PHP error log, and the layer will be removed in Fegg 6.

searchDocs.title: Where to start​
searchDocs.content: Directory structure: what lives in core/ and site/Settings: site/config/settings.php, env.php and the database connectionfegg-cli: command line toolsUpdating the coreMigrating a Fegg 3 / 4 projectURL and Controller: how a request reaches your codeSecurity and Logging and errors

searchDocs.title: Config​
searchDocs.content: Load config files from site/config/ and read the settings.  📄️Application::loadConfig Load a config file 📄️Application::getSetting Get a value from the settings

searchDocs.title: Ticket​
searchDocs.content: A ticket protects form processing. setTicket() creates a random string, stores it in the session and adds it to the form as a hidden field (output with {{ hidden }}). When the form is posted, useTicket() checks that the posted value matches the session and then removes it, so the same form cannot be processed twice.  📄️Application::setTicket Issue a one-time ticket for a form 📄️Application::useTicket Check a one-time ticket and use it up

searchDocs.title: Redirect​
searchDocs.content: redirect() ends the response by throwing Fegg\Http\Halt, like displayPage(). Never write exit in a controller; use $this->halt() (see Ending a response).

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public mixed Application::getSetting( string $name )   Get a value of $settings: the defaults in core/config/settings.php, overridden by site/config/settings.php (see Settings). Returns '' when the key does not exist.  Project-specific keys work too: add them to site/config/settings.php and read them with getSetting().

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$name	string Setting key

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: htdocs/_fegg/site/config/settings.php $settings['developer_ip'] = array('192.168.65.1'); // A project-specific setting $settings['contact_admin_email'] = 'info@example.com';   Controller var_dump($this->getSetting('developer_ip')); // -> array(1) { [0]=> string(12) "192.168.65.1" } echo $this->getSetting('contact_admin_email'); // -> info@example.com echo $this->getSetting('no_such_key'); // -> ''

searchDocs.title: Application log​
searchDocs.content: Fegg\Log writes one line per entry to htdocs/_fegg/site/data/log/fegg-YYYY-MM-DD.log. Call it from anywhere (controllers, your classes in site/src/):  Controller use Fegg\Log; Log::info('Import finished', array('rows' => $count)); Log::warning('Unknown category {id}', array('id' => $id)); try { $this->_import($file); } catch (\Exception $e) { Log::error('Import failed for {file}', array('file' => $name, 'exception' => $e)); }   site/data/log/fegg-2026-11-10.log [2026-11-10 12:34:56 +09:00] ERROR Import failed for news.csv {"file":"news.csv","exception":"RuntimeException: Bad line 3 at /path/Import.php:42"} | POST /cms/import/ 203.0.113.5   {key} in the message is replaced with $context['key']. The context is appended as JSON; an exception is written as its class, message, file and line.For web requests the line ends with the method, the URL and the visitor's address.The method names are the PSR-3 levels, from lowest to highest: debug, info, notice, warning, error, critical, alert, emergency. Each returns true when the entry was written.Never log passwords, tokens or full personal data.

searchDocs.title: Settings​
searchDocs.content: Setting	Default	Remarks$settings['log_level']	''	Lowest level written. '': warning in production, debug elsewhere (FEGG_ENV) $settings['log_retention_days']	30	Files older than this are removed. 0: keep all FEGG_LOG_DIR (env.php or environment variable)	site/data/log	Directory of the log files  htdocs/_fegg/site/config/settings.php $settings['log_level'] = 'info'; $settings['log_retention_days'] = 90;   site/data/ is not tracked by git and is denied to the web by htdocs/_fegg/.htaccess.

searchDocs.title: Uncaught errors​
searchDocs.content: An exception or error that no code catches (a Fegg\Database\QueryException, a missing template, a PHP error ...) ends the request with HTTP 500:  It is written to the PHP error log and to the application log, with the stack trace and, for errors raised by a template, the .tpl file and line (Template: news/detail.tpl:12).In developer mode the details are shown in the browser.Everyone else gets the error page core/template/error/500.html. What a half-rendered page already printed is discarded.  To use your own design, put a file at htdocs/_fegg/site/template/error/500.html. It is plain HTML, not a template (no {{ }} tags, no includes), so it still works when the templates or the database are what broke. Inline its CSS or link to files under htdocs/data/.  Catch an exception only when the page can do something useful with it; otherwise let it reach the 500 page and the log. When you catch \Throwable, rethrow Fegg\Http\Halt (see Ending a response).

searchDocs.title: Requests to other services​
searchDocs.content: Fegg\Http\Client is a small HTTP client for calling other services. Fegg itself uses it for the captcha checks, oEmbed and fegg-cli doctor.  Controller use Fegg\Http\Client; use Fegg\Http\ClientException; use Fegg\Log; $client = new Client(10, 3); // seconds for the whole request, seconds to connect try { $response = $client->get('https://api.example.com/items?category=2', array('Accept: application/json')); if ($response['status'] === 200) { $items = json_decode($response['body'], true); } $response = $client->post('https://api.example.com/entries', array('name' => $name)); } catch (ClientException $e) { Log::warning('API not reachable: {message}', array('message' => $e->getMessage())); }   get($url, $headers = array()) and post($url, $body, $headers = array()) return array('status' => int, 'body' => string). A $body array is sent as application/x-www-form-urlencoded; a string is sent as is (set the Content-Type header yourself, for JSON for example).A response with an error status (404, 500 ...) is returned normally: check status. Only a transport failure (no connection, timeout) throws Fegg\Http\ClientException.Only http and https URLs are accepted (anything else throws InvalidArgumentException), and redirects are not followed.It uses cURL when the extension is installed, otherwise PHP's http stream wrapper.

searchDocs.title: Mail​
searchDocs.content: Fegg\Tool\Mail sends through sendmail unless $settings['mail'] selects SMTP, with the password in env.php as FEGG_SMTP_PASSWORD. See Mail.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public array Application::loadConfig( string $name, string $languageCode = '' )   Load the config file {$name}.php, store its variable in $this->config[$name] and return it.  The file must define a variable with the same name as the file (sample.php defines $sample). It is searched in this order, and the first file found is loaded:  htdocs/_fegg/site/config/{$name}.phphtdocs/_fegg/core/config/{$name}.php  So a site file replaces the core file with the same name (for example validation_error_message.php). If global_config_dir is set in the settings, the file in that directory is loaded first and the file above can overwrite its values.  On a multilingual site (default_language and support_language are set), config/{language code}/{$name}.php is loaded afterwards and can overwrite values for that language.  The result is cached: calling loadConfig() again with the same name returns $this->config[$name] without reading the file. If no file defines the variable, Fegg prints Can't Read Config File: {$name} and stops.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$name	string Config file name without .php (also the name of the variable the file defines) $languageCode	string	''	Language code for the per-language file. The current language when omitted

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: htdocs/_fegg/site/config/sample.php <?php defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; // The variable name must be the same as the file name $sample = array(); $sample['foo'] = 'bar'; $sample['baz'] = 'qux';   Controller $this->loadConfig('sample'); var_dump($this->config['sample']);   Output array(2) { ["foo"]=> string(3) "bar" ["baz"]=> string(3) "qux" }   The return value can also be used directly:  Controller $sample = $this->loadConfig('sample'); echo $sample['foo']; // -> bar   site_info.php and category_info.php are loaded by the base controller's __init(), so $this->config['site_info'] and $this->config['category_info'] are available in every controller that calls parent::__init().

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public void Application::redirect( string $url )   Send a Location header (HTTP 302) and end the response. Code after redirect() is not run.  redirect() does not call exit: it throws Fegg\Http\Halt, which the dispatcher catches before it writes the session and sends the response. There is no need to write exit after it. A catch (\Throwable $e) around redirect() must rethrow Fegg\Http\Halt (see Ending a response); catch (\Exception $e) is not affected.  A URL starting with http:// or https:// is used as is.Any other URL is a path inside the site. A / is added at the start if missing, a trailing / is added when the path has no extension (to avoid a second redirect, see URL), and the current protocol, domain and base path are added in front. This also works when the site is installed in a subdirectory.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$url	string Absolute URL, or a path inside the site

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller // -> https://example.com/news/ $this->redirect('/news/'); // -> https://example.com/news/ (slashes added) $this->redirect('news'); // -> https://example.com/contact/result.html $this->redirect('/contact/result.html'); // -> https://www.example.org/ $this->redirect('https://www.example.org/');   Do not pass a URL taken from the request (for example $this->in('return_to')) without checking it, or the site becomes an open redirect.

searchDocs.title: Inside try / catch​
searchDocs.content: Controller try { $this->_save($data); $this->redirect('/entry/done/'); } catch (\Fegg\Http\Halt $halt) { throw $halt; } catch (\Throwable $e) { \Fegg\Log::error('Entry could not be saved', array('exception' => $e)); $this->redirect('/entry/error/'); }

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public bool Application::useTicket( string $name )   Check the ticket issued by Application::setTicket. Returns true only when the POST parameter ticket_{$name} has the same value as the ticket in the session. The ticket is then removed from the session, so a second submit of the same form returns false.  The ticket is read from POST only.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$name	string Ticket name

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller public function result() { if (!$this->useTicket('contact')) { // Reloaded, submitted twice, or not posted from the form $this->redirect('/contact/'); } // send the mail ... $this->displayPage('contact/result'); }

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public void Application::setTicket( string $name )   Issue a one-time ticket (a random string) for a form. The ticket is stored in the session as ticket_{$name}, and the same value is registered as a hidden field named ticket_{$name}. Output it in the form with the {{ hidden }} template tag.  When the form is submitted, check it with Application::useTicket. This prevents the same form from being processed twice (reload, double submit) and rejects posts that did not come from your form page.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$name	string Ticket name

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller public function confirm() { $this->setTicket('contact'); $this->displayPage('contact/confirm'); }   Controller echo $this->getSession('ticket_contact');   Output 670f2f1232f30d4d716c1bc9c8a58388   Template: contact/confirm.tpl <form method="post" action="{{ base }}/contact/result.html"> {{ hidden }} <button type="submit">Send</button> </form>   Output <form method="post" action="/contact/result.html"> <input type="hidden" name="ticket_contact" value="670f2f1232f30d4d716c1bc9c8a58388"> <button type="submit">Send</button> </form>   {{ hidden }} outputs every value registered with setHidden(), so other hidden values appear there too.

searchDocs.title: POST/GET​
searchDocs.content: Get request data. Values are returned as sent: validate them, and let the template escape them on output.  📄️Application::in Get request data (POST/GET)

searchDocs.title: SESSION​
searchDocs.content: Set and read SESSION data. Never call session_start() yourself: Fegg starts the session only when something is written to it (setSession(), setTicket(), the CMS). Reading with getSession() or {{ $session }} on a request without a session cookie returns nothing and starts nothing, so ordinary public pages send no Set-Cookie and can be cached.  The session cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax. It is Secure when the request is HTTPS (also behind a proxy that sends X-Forwarded-Proto: https).session.use_strict_mode is on: a session ID the server did not issue is replaced by a new one.The session is written when the response ends: after displayPage(), redirect(), $this->halt() or the end of the method (see Ending a response).  📄️Application::setSession Set SESSION data (and start the session) 📄️Application::getSession Get SESSION data 📄️Application::unsetSession Unset SESSION data 📄️Application::regenerateSessionId Give the session a new ID

searchDocs.title: COOKIE​
searchDocs.content: Set and read COOKIE data. Cookies set with setCookie() are HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict by default and Secure over HTTPS.  📄️Application::setCookie Set COOKIE data 📄️Application::getCookie Get COOKIE data 📄️Application::unsetCookie Delete a cookie

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public void Application::setCookie( string $name, string $value, int $expire = '', string $path = '/', string $sameSite = 'Strict' )   Set COOKIE data. The cookie is always HttpOnly (JavaScript cannot read it). It is Secure (sent back over HTTPS only) when the request is HTTPS, or when $sameSite is None, which browsers require. Over plain HTTP, on a local development server for example, it works without Secure.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$name	string Cookie name $value	string Value $expire	int	''	Lifetime in seconds from now. When omitted (or 0), 1 week (604800 seconds) $path	string	'/'	Path where the cookie is valid $sameSite	string	'Strict'	SameSite attribute: Strict, Lax or None

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: If you omit the third argument, the cookie expires after 1 week.  Controller $this->setCookie('foo', 'bar');   Set the lifetime in seconds with the third argument.  Controller // This cookie expires after 60 seconds. $this->setCookie('foo', 'bar', 60);   Set the path with the fourth argument and the SameSite attribute with the fifth.  Controller // This cookie is only valid under "/test/". $this->setCookie('foo', 'bar', 0, '/test/'); // Sent back when the visitor follows a link from another site (SameSite=Lax) $this->setCookie('campaign', 'spring', 86400 * 30, '/', 'Lax');   note Fegg 4 passed SameSite inside the path ('/test/; SameSite=Lax'). That form still works: the attribute is taken out of the path and used as $sameSite.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public void Application::unsetCookie( string $name )   Delete the cookie: it is sent again with an expiry date in the past (path /), so the browser drops it. It is also removed from getCookie() for the rest of the current request. From the next request on, the browser no longer sends it.  Only cookies with the path / are deleted. Fegg 4 set an empty cookie for seven days instead.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$name	string Cookie name

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller - First request $this->setCookie('foo', 'bar');   Controller - Second request echo $this->getCookie('foo'); // -> bar $this->unsetCookie('foo');   Controller - Third request echo $this->getCookie('foo'); // -> ''

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public string|array Application::in( string $name = '', string $method = '' )   Get request data from $_GET and $_POST.  With $name, returns the value of that parameter (a string, or an array for parameters like ids[]). If the parameter is missing or an empty string, returns ''.Without $name, returns all parameters as an array ('' when there are none).If GET and POST have a parameter with the same name, POST wins.  The value is returned as it was sent. It is not escaped: validate it before use, pass it to the database only through ? placeholders, and let the template escape it on output.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$name	string	''	Request parameter name. All parameters when omitted $method	string	''	'get' or 'post' (case-insensitive) to read only one of them. Both when omitted

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller - GET // https://example.com/?foo=get echo $this->in('foo'); // -> get echo $this->in('foo', 'get'); // -> get echo $this->in('foo', 'post'); // -> '' (empty string)   Controller - POST // https://example.com/ : POST('foo' => 'post') echo $this->in('foo'); // -> post echo $this->in('foo', 'get'); // -> '' echo $this->in('foo', 'post'); // -> post   If POST and GET have a parameter with the same name, POST wins.  Controller - GET and POST // https://example.com/?foo=get : POST('foo' => 'post') echo $this->in('foo'); // -> post echo $this->in('foo', 'get'); // -> get echo $this->in('foo', 'post'); // -> post   You can get all request data by omitting the first argument.  Controller // https://example.com/ : POST('foo' => 'bar', 'baz' => 'qux') var_dump( $this->in() );   Output array(2) { ["foo"]=> string(3) "bar" ["baz"]=> string(3) "qux" }   A typical use is the page number of a list:  htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/News.php $this->page['data'] = $this->_model ->listMax(20) ->current($this->in('p')) ->order('post_date', 'desc') ->find();

searchDocs.title: What is a Controller?​
searchDocs.content: A controller is the class that handles a request. Fegg picks the controller class and its method from the URL (see URL).  https://example.com/foo/bar/   For this URL, Fegg loads htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/Foo.php and calls its bar() method:  htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/Foo.php <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; class Foo extends Controller { public function bar() { // process here... } }

searchDocs.title: File, namespace and class​
searchDocs.content: Every controller file follows the same rules:  The file is in htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/, and the file name is the class name (Foo.php declares class Foo).The namespace is Site\Controller. Sub directories are namespaces: site/controller/Cms/News.php declares namespace Site\Controller\Cms; and class News.The first line after the namespace is defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit;. It is required in every PHP file under htdocs/_fegg/: it stops the file from running when someone requests it directly by URL.The class extends Controller, the project's base class.  htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/Cms/News.php <?php namespace Site\Controller\Cms; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Cms\Helper; use Fegg\Model; use Site\Controller\Controller; // the base class is in the parent namespace class News extends Controller { // ... }

searchDocs.title: Base classes​
searchDocs.content: There are two kinds of controllers, with a base class each: public pages and CMS screens.  Fegg\Application core/src/Application.php └ Fegg\Controller\Controller (abstract) core/controller/Controller.php ├ Site\Controller\Controller (abstract) site/controller/Controller.php public pages │ └ Site\Controller\Index, News, Contact, ... └ Fegg\Controller\Cms\Controller (abstract) core/controller/Cms/Controller.php CMS screens (core) ├ Fegg\Controller\Cms\Image, Media, Login, ... └ Site\Controller\Cms\Controller (abstract) site/controller/Cms/Controller.php CMS screens (project) └ Site\Controller\Cms\News, Lab, ...   Fegg\Application provides the methods you call with $this->...: request parameters, templates (displayPage(), ...), redirect(), loadConfig(), ...Fegg\Controller\Controller (core) loads site/config/category_info.php and site/config/site_info.php in its __init(), and declares the properties $_model and $_lh used by the CMS.

searchDocs.title: Which methods are actions​
searchDocs.content: Only a controller's own actions can be called from a URL. A method is an action when it is:  public and not static,declared in the controller itself (or a parent that is not one of the base classes above). Methods declared in Fegg\Controller\Controller, Site\Controller\Controller and the two CMS base classes are never actions, even when a controller overrides them,not named like a method of Fegg\Application: mail, in, redirect, halt, setSession, setCookie, displayPage ... are 404 as URL segments,not starting with _ (__init(), _validatePostedData()).  Anything else answers 404. Put shared helpers in a base class as protected methods, and write an action used by several controllers in each of them (it can call a shared helper). Fegg 4 called any method the controller had, including setSession() and mail() of the framework: this is a Fegg 5 change.  Site\Controller\Controller (site) is yours: the base of the public pages. Put what every public page needs here (shared assigns, ...). It replaces MyApplication of Fegg 4.Fegg\Controller\Cms\Controller (core) and Site\Controller\Cms\Controller (site) are the bases of the CMS screens: see CMS screens. Put what every CMS screen of the project needs in Site\Controller\Cms\Controller.  htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/Controller.php <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; abstract class Controller extends \Fegg\Controller\Controller { public function __init() { parent::__init(); // Shared by every page of the site $this->page['year'] = date('Y'); } }   Abstract classes are never called from a URL.

searchDocs.title: Constructor​
searchDocs.content: A constructor is optional. If you write one, call the parent constructor: it loads the settings, sets up error handling and the language.  public function __construct() { parent::__construct(); }

searchDocs.title: Initialize​
searchDocs.content: __init() is called after the constructor, before the method of the URL. Because the instance already exists, you can use the Application methods through $this (for example $this->in()), which you should not do in the constructor.  Always call parent::__init() first. Otherwise site_info.php and category_info.php are not loaded.  public function __init() { parent::__init(); $this->_lh = new Helper(); $this->_model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); }   note You can omit __init() when the controller does not need it. The parent __init() is then called automatically.

searchDocs.title: Method​
searchDocs.content: The second segment of the URL is the method name.  // Called by https://example.com/foo/bar/ public function bar() { // any process }   If the second segment is empty, index() is called.  // Called by https://example.com/foo/ or https://example.com/foo/index/ public function index() { // any process }   Every public method can be called from a URL. Make helper methods private or protected so that they cannot.  // https://example.com/foo/_common/ does NOT run this method private function _common() { // shared process }   If the method does not exist, the 404 page is shown.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: The segments after the method are passed to the method as strings.  // $param1 is "bar" and $param2 is "baz" // for https://example.com/foo/show/bar/baz/ public function show($param1 = '', $param2 = '') { echo $param1; // bar echo $param2; // baz }   Give the arguments a default value: a visitor can always open the URL with fewer segments, and a missing required argument is an error (HTTP 500).

searchDocs.title: Ending a response​
searchDocs.content: displayPage(), redirect(), requirePost(), Basic authentication and the CMS login check end the response by throwing Fegg\Http\Halt. The dispatcher catches it, writes the session and sends the output. Code after them does not run, as before, but Fegg 5 never calls exit.  To stop a controller yourself, call $this->halt() instead of exit. It prints its argument, if any, and ends the response the same way:  public function ping() { header('Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8'); $this->halt('pong'); // not: echo 'pong'; exit; }   With halt() the dispatcher finishes the request itself (it writes the session and sends the buffered output), and the code stays testable. exit still stops the script, but skips all of that.  Halt extends \Error, not \Exception, so catch (\Exception $e) does not stop a redirect. A catch (\Throwable $e) around displayPage() or redirect() would catch it: rethrow it first.  try { $this->_import($file); $this->redirect('/cms/import/done/'); } catch (\Fegg\Http\Halt $halt) { throw $halt; // the redirect: let it through } catch (\Throwable $e) { \Fegg\Log::error('Import failed', array('exception' => $e)); $this->displayPage('cms/import/error'); }

searchDocs.title: Using other classes​
searchDocs.content: Classes are autoloaded. Import them with use, or write the full name with a leading \, and create them with new:  use Fegg\Cms\Helper; use Fegg\Model; use Fegg\Validation; $this->_lh = new Helper('news'); $validation = new Validation(); $upload = new \Fegg\Tool\Upload(); $cart = new \Site\Shop\Cart(); // htdocs/_fegg/site/src/Shop/Cart.php   Inside a namespace, prefix PHP's own classes and constants with \. Without it, PHP looks for the class in the current namespace (Site\Controller\Exception) and fails.  throw new \Exception('Something went wrong'); $date = new \DateTime('now'); $statement->bindValue(1, $id, \PDO::PARAM_INT);   Catch Fegg's exceptions by their full name, for example \Fegg\Database\QueryException or \Fegg\Template\TemplateException.  note $this->getClass() still works for Fegg 4 code, but it is deprecated (each call writes Fegg deprecated: ... to the PHP error log) and will be removed in Fegg 6.

searchDocs.title: Extending a core controller​
searchDocs.content: The CMS screens provided by the core (/cms/login/, /cms/media/, /cms/image/, ...) are in htdocs/_fegg/core/controller/Cms/. Do not edit them. To change one, put a class with the same name in site/controller/Cms/ that extends the core class, and write only the methods you change. The site class is found first, so it replaces the core one for its URL.  htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/Cms/Media.php <?php namespace Site\Controller\Cms; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; // Changes only the /cms/media/ list class Media extends \Fegg\Controller\Cms\Media { public function index($message = null) { // project-specific processing parent::index($message); } }   Keep the parent method's signature (the same arguments with the same defaults).

searchDocs.title: CMS screens​
searchDocs.content: A CMS screen extends Site\Controller\Cms\Controller (in site/controller/Cms/, where Controller is that class without a use). Before your method runs, the base class:  sends a visitor who is not logged in to the login page,creates $this->_lh (Fegg\Cms\Helper) for the section set in $_cmsSection, and sets $this->page['prefix'] and $this->page['prev_num'],sends Cache-Control: no-store and X-Robots-Tag: noindex,checks the CSRF token of every POST request: a POST without the session's token gets a 403 page.  Every action that changes data calls requirePost() first The CSRF token is only checked on POST. An action that saves, deletes or sorts must start with $this->requirePost(): without it, the action also runs on a GET, so a link or an image on another site can change data while a CMS user is logged in. With it, a GET gets a 405. This is new in Fegg 5. CMS controllers copied from a Fegg 4 project do not have it: add it to every update, create, delete ... (see Migrating from v3 / v4).  htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/Cms/Event.php <?php namespace Site\Controller\Cms; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Model; class Event extends Controller { // The URL segment under /cms/ (/cms/event/...) protected $_cmsSection = 'event'; public function __init() { parent::__init(); $this->_model = new Model(true, array('table' => 'cms_event', 'id' => 'event_id')); } public function update() { // Required in every action that changes data (a link or a URL typed in the browser gets a 405) $this->requirePost(); // validate $this->in('title', 'POST') ..., then insertRow() / updateRow() } public function delete($internalId) { $this->requirePost(); $this->_model->delete($internalId); $this->redirect($this->_lh->getBackPath('index/DELETED')); } }

searchDocs.title: Forms and the CSRF token​
searchDocs.content: A form that prints {{ hidden }} sends the token already (the base class adds it to the hidden values).Any other POST form adds it with {{ include '/cms/parts/csrf' }}.Delete buttons are small POST forms, not links. link-alert asks for confirmation before sending:  htdocs/_fegg/site/template/cms/event/lists.tpl <form class="link-alert" action="{{ $site.prefix }}/delete/{{ $post[$page.this_id] }}" method="post" data-message="削除してもよろしいですか？" style="display: inline;"> {{ include '/cms/parts/csrf' }} <button type="submit" class="c-button is-micro is-danger">削除</button> </form>   JavaScript can read the token from <meta name="csrf-token"> and send it as the cms_csrf POST field.The token is the same for the whole session (several tabs work) and changes when you log in.

searchDocs.title: Login and logout​
searchDocs.content: The login screens are core controllers (Fegg\Controller\Cms\Login, Logout):  /cms/login/auth accepts POST only. Deleted users (valid = 0) cannot log in, and old password hashes are upgraded at login.Every CMS request checks that the session's user still exists in cms_user (valid = 1): deleting a user ends their sessions at once.Login throttling: every attempt is recorded before the password is checked. After 5 failed logins for one login ID from one address, or 20 from one address, logins from that address are refused for 15 minutes. The failures are stored in the core table cms_login_attempt: run fegg-cli migration after updating. Without the table the login still works, unthrottled, and a warning is logged.Logout is a POST with the CSRF token, so another site cannot log a user out. /cms/logout/ opened as a link shows a logout button; links with the class js-cms-logout post directly (htdocs/cms/js/base.js). If you copied the CMS frame templates to site/template/cms/, add that class to the logout link.CMS users are created with fegg-cli user:create. /cms/register/ needs a CMS login and developer mode.

searchDocs.title: Template of Controller class​
searchDocs.content: htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/Index.php <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Cms\Helper; use Fegg\Model; /** * Index Class * This file name should be Index.php */ class Index extends Controller { /** * Initialize * Runs after the constructor, so Application methods such as $this->in() can be used. * Optional. Always call parent::__init() first. */ public function __init() { parent::__init(); $this->_lh = new Helper(); $this->_model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); } /** * Shared process * Private, so it cannot be called from a URL. */ private function _common() { } /** * Default page * Called when the URL has no method segment. */ public function index() { $this->_common(); $this->page['news'] = $this->_model ->order('post_date', 'desc') ->limit(5) ->all(); // Display the compiled template site/template/index.tpl $this->displayPage('index'); } }

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public string|array Application::getCookie( string $name = '' )   Get COOKIE data sent by the browser. If the cookie does not exist, returns ''. If you omit the argument, returns all COOKIE data as an array.  Cookies set with setCookie() are sent back by the browser from the next request on; getCookie() does not see them in the same request.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$name	string	''	Cookie name. All COOKIE data when omitted

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller - First request $this->setCookie('foo', 'bar');   Controller - Second request echo $this->getCookie('foo'); // -> bar

searchDocs.title: Get all cookie data​
searchDocs.content: If you omit the argument, getCookie returns all COOKIE data.  Controller - First request $this->setCookie('foo', 'bar'); $this->setCookie('baz', 'qux');   Controller - Second request var_dump( $this->getCookie() );   Output array(2) { ["foo"]=> string(3) "bar" ["baz"]=> string(3) "qux" }   The array also contains the other cookies of the site, such as the session cookie.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public void Application::regenerateSessionId()   Replace the current session ID with a new one and delete the old session file (session_regenerate_id(true)). The SESSION data is kept. Starts the session if it has not been started.  Call it whenever the user's privileges change, typically right after a successful login, so that a session ID obtained before the login cannot be used afterwards (session fixation).

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: None.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller // _findUser() is your own private method that checks the login ID and password $user = $this->_findUser($this->in('login_id', 'post'), $this->in('password', 'post')); if ($user) { $this->regenerateSessionId(); $this->setSession('user_id', $user['user_id']); $this->redirect('/mypage/'); }

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public mixed Application::getSession( string $name = '' )   Get SESSION data. If the key does not exist, returns ''. If you omit the argument, returns all SESSION data as an array.  getSession() does not create a session: when the request has no session cookie (and nothing was written to the session yet), it returns '' (or array() without an argument) and no cookie is sent. An existing session is opened to read it.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$name	string	''	Session key. All SESSION data when omitted

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller - First request $this->setSession('foo', 'bar');   Controller - Second request echo $this->getSession('foo'); // -> bar echo $this->getSession('none'); // -> '' (empty string)

searchDocs.title: Get all session data​
searchDocs.content: If you omit the argument, getSession returns all SESSION data.  Controller - First request $this->setSession('foo', 'bar'); $this->setSession('baz', 'qux');   Controller - Second request var_dump( $this->getSession() );   Output array(2) { ["foo"]=> string(3) "bar" ["baz"]=> string(3) "qux" }

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public void Application::unsetSession( string $name = '' )   Remove one key from the SESSION data. If you omit the argument, unsetSession removes all SESSION data, destroys the session and deletes the session cookie (use it to log a user out). Without a session it does nothing.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$name	string	''	Session key. Destroys the whole session and its cookie when omitted

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller - First request $this->setSession('foo', 'bar');   Controller - Second request echo $this->getSession('foo'); // -> bar   Controller - Third request $this->unsetSession('foo'); echo $this->getSession('foo'); // -> ''

searchDocs.title: Remove all session data​
searchDocs.content: If you omit the argument, unsetSession removes all SESSION data, destroys the session and deletes the session cookie.  Controller - First request $this->setSession('foo', 'bar'); $this->setSession('baz', 'qux');   Controller - Second request $this->unsetSession(); echo $this->getSession('foo'); // -> '' echo $this->getSession('baz'); // -> ''

searchDocs.title: About Template​
searchDocs.content: Fegg has its own template engine that keeps the application code (PHP) apart from the display (HTML/CSS). A template (.tpl) is HTML with {{ ... }} tags. Fegg compiles it to PHP, caches the result and runs it when a controller displays the page.  htdocs/_fegg/site/template/news/detail.tpl {{ transclude '/template/siteframe' }} {{ section contents }} <h1>{{ $page.data.title }}</h1> <p>{{ $page.data.post_date|feggDate:'Y/m/d' }}</p> {{ end section contents }}

searchDocs.title: Where templates live​
searchDocs.content: Directory	Ownerhtdocs/_fegg/site/template/	The project. Put your templates here. htdocs/_fegg/core/template/	The core (CMS screens). Never edit it: it is replaced by fegg-cli core:update.  Templates are looked up in site/template/ first, then in core/template/. To change a core template, copy it to the same path under site/template/ and edit the copy: the project file wins.  Template names never include the .tpl extension. A controller renders site/template/news/detail.tpl with:  htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/News.php $this->displayPage('news/detail');   When the site is multi-language (default_language and support_language are set in the settings), the language code is put in front of the name: news/detail is read from site/template/<language code>/news/detail.tpl.

searchDocs.title: Paths in include and transclude​
searchDocs.content: A path starting with / is relative to the template root (site/template/, then core/template/). It works the same in a template at any depth. Prefer it.Any other path is relative to the directory of the template that contains the tag (./parts/card, ../template/siteframe).  {{ transclude '/template/siteframe' }} site/template/template/siteframe.tpl {{ transclude '/cms/frame/siteframe' }} core/template/cms/frame/siteframe.tpl (CMS screens) {{ include head '/include/head/about' }} site/template/include/head/about.tpl {{ include './parts/card' }} parts/card.tpl next to this template

searchDocs.title: Cache​
searchDocs.content: Compiled templates are cached in htdocs/_fegg/site/data/cache/template/, which must be writable by the web server. A cache file is rebuilt automatically when the template, one of its transclude parents or the template compiler changes (any change of modification time or size), so you never need to clear it by hand.

searchDocs.title: Checking templates​
searchDocs.content: After writing or editing a template, run:  ./fegg-cli template:lint   It compiles every template without running it and reports unknown tags, unclosed blocks, missing include / transclude targets, undefined modifiers and unsafe outputs, with the .tpl line. See Lint and errors.

searchDocs.title: Display methods​
searchDocs.content: Display methods render a template from a controller. Use displayPage for pages: it sets the variables templates expect and protects against clickjacking.  📄️Application::displayPage Display a page with the standard template variables and end the response 📄️Application::fetchPage Return a page rendered with the standard template variables as a string 📄️Application::displayTemplate Output a template with only the variables you pass 📄️Application::fetchTemplate Return a template rendered with only the variables you pass, as a string

searchDocs.title: Template helper methods​
searchDocs.content: Template helper methods pass special values (site information, hidden inputs, HTTP headers) from the controller.  📄️Application::setSiteinfo Set website information (title, description, keywords …) 📄️Application::setHidden Set values for hidden inputs 📄️Application::setHtmlHeader Send an HTTP response header

searchDocs.title: Template rules​
searchDocs.content: The tags you can write in a template.  📄️Variable Output variables 📄️Assign Set a variable in the template 📄️If if, else if, else 📄️Loop foreach, loop 📄️Include include, include head, head, include foot, foot, include html 📄️Transclude transclude, section 📄️Base URL base, baseurl, currenturl 📄️Checked/Selected checked, selected 📄️Options Make option tags 📄️Hidden Output hidden inputs 📄️Code Run a PHP statement 📄️Call Run a controller method 📄️Comment Template comments 📄️Literal braces Output {{ and }} as text

searchDocs.title: Modifiers, security and lint​
searchDocs.content: Modifiers transform a value before it is output. The security page explains which escaping each place in the HTML needs, and the lint page lists every check of fegg-cli template:lint and how template errors are reported.  📄️Modifiers Modifiers transform a value before it is output. 📄️Security Escaping by context, and templates as code 📄️Lint and errors Check templates with fegg-cli template:lint, and find the template line of an error

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public void Application::setSession( string $name, mixed $value )   Set SESSION data. Starts the session if it has not been started, so you never call session_start() yourself. Writing is what starts a session: a page that never calls setSession() (or setTicket()) sends no session cookie.  The session cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, and Secure over HTTPS. The data is saved when the response ends (displayPage(), redirect(), $this->halt(), or the end of the method).

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$name	string Session key $value	mixed Value

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $this->setSession('foo', 'bar'); $this->setSession('cart', array('item_id' => 3, 'quantity' => 1));

searchDocs.title: Secrets and environments​
searchDocs.content: Passwords, API keys and anything else that differs per server are not committed. Put them in htdocs/_fegg/site/config/env.php (in .gitignore; copy env.php.dist) or in environment variables, and read them with feggEnv('NAME', $default). See Settings.  htdocs/_fegg/site/config/env.php <?php defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; return array( 'FEGG_ENV' => 'production', 'FEGG_DB_PASSWORD' => '...', 'FEGG_RECAPTCHA_SECRET' => '...', 'FEGG_SMTP_PASSWORD' => '...', );   A site without env.php runs as production: no error details on screen, for anyone. Test servers whose project path matches site/config/env/paths.php (the LionHeart develop server) use the committed site/config/env/staging.php instead: it holds only test values, never production secrets (Test servers deployed with git pull).Environments are chosen by the server's path, never by the request's host name, which the client controls.Error details are shown only in developer mode: a developer_ip address and FEGG_ENV other than production. developer_ip alone is not a security boundary: behind a proxy or load balancer every request may come from the same address.

searchDocs.title: Security headers​
searchDocs.content: Every response (pages, redirects, 404, error pages, the CMS) gets these headers. The bootstrap sends them before the controller runs.  Header	Default	Setting in site/config/settings.phpX-Content-Type-Options	nosniff	$settings['security_headers'] Referrer-Policy	strict-origin-when-cross-origin	$settings['security_headers'] X-Frame-Options	SAMEORIGIN (the CMS image and file pickers are iframes)	$settings['security_headers']; $this->allowFraming() for one response Strict-Transport-Security	not sent	$settings['hsts'] (sent on HTTPS responses only) Content-Security-Policy	not sent	$settings['csp']; $settings['csp_report_only'] = true sends it as Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only  htdocs/_fegg/site/config/settings.php // Change or remove a default ('' removes it), or add another header $settings['security_headers'] = array( 'Referrer-Policy' => 'same-origin', 'Permissions-Policy' => 'camera=(), microphone=()', ); // Only once the whole site redirects to HTTPS (and every subdomain, with includeSubDomains) $settings['hsts'] = 'max-age=31536000'; // Try a policy in report-only mode first $settings['csp'] = "default-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; script-src 'self' https://www.google.com https://www.gstatic.com"; $settings['csp_report_only'] = true;   Turn HSTS on only when every page is served over HTTPS: browsers then refuse HTTP for that domain for max-age seconds.A CSP must list inline scripts and every external service the site uses (analytics, reCAPTCHA, Turnstile, YouTube ...). Watch the browser console in report-only mode before you enforce it.A page that other sites may show in a frame (an embeddable widget) calls $this->allowFraming() before displayPage(). It removes X-Frame-Options for that response only.

searchDocs.title: Sessions and cookies​
searchDocs.content: A session starts only when something is written to it (setSession(), setTicket(), the CMS). Reading does not create one, so ordinary public pages send no Set-Cookie.The session cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, and Secure when the request is HTTPS (also behind a proxy that sends X-Forwarded-Proto: https).session.use_strict_mode is on: a session ID the server did not issue is replaced.Call regenerateSessionId() after a login. unsetSession() without a name ends the session and deletes its cookie.setCookie() sets HttpOnly cookies, SameSite=Strict by default, Secure over HTTPS. unsetCookie() deletes one.

searchDocs.title: Forms​
searchDocs.content: Output escaping: {{ $x }} escapes HTML. In URLs and JavaScript use feggUrl and feggJs; ./fegg-cli template:lint reports outputs without them. See Template security.Double submission: public forms use tickets (setTicket() / useTicket()). The skeleton's contact form revokes the ticket when a confirmation fails, and sends the auto-reply to exactly one address.CSRF in the CMS: every POST to a CMS screen must carry the session's token, or it gets a 403. Every action that changes data must call $this->requirePost() first: the token is only checked on POST, so an action without it can be triggered by a link on another site. A GET then gets a 405, and deletes are small POST forms, not links. See Controller.Actions: only a controller's own public methods can be called from a URL, never the framework's (setSession(), mail() ...). See Controller.Database: values always go through ? placeholders. Table, column and order names are checked by Fegg\Model and must never come from user input.Spam: the contact form supports reCAPTCHA and Turnstile. When the service cannot be reached the check fails, it is never skipped (see Captcha).

searchDocs.title: CMS login​
searchDocs.content: After 5 failed logins for one login ID from one address, or 20 from one address, logins from that address are refused for 15 minutes. The failures are kept in the core table cms_login_attempt: run fegg-cli migration after updating the core. Without the table the login works unthrottled and a warning is logged./cms/login/auth is POST only. Deleted users (valid = 0) cannot log in, and deleting a user ends their sessions. Old password hashes are upgraded at login. An unknown login ID takes as long to check as a wrong password.Logout is a POST with the CSRF token (see Controller).Users are created and their passwords changed with fegg-cli user:create / user:password, which never take the password on the command line. /cms/register/ needs a CMS login and developer mode.Basic authentication compares the user and password with hash_equals(). With basic_auth_scope = 1 it is checked before the controller's __init() and action, so redirects, downloads and direct output are protected too.

searchDocs.title: Uploads​
searchDocs.content: The extension must be allowed, and script extensions (php, phtml, phar, cgi ...) are always refused.The content must match the extension (getimagesize() for images, finfo for known types): a script renamed to .jpg is refused.Directories are created 0755, files 0644. Files are saved under generated names.The upload directory below the document root gets an .htaccess that stops scripts from running. fegg-cli doctor reports a missing htdocs/up_dir/.htaccess. On nginx, deny scripts under the upload URL yourself.Stored files are sent with nosniff and an escaped Content-Disposition; HTML, SVG and XML are always attachments.  See Upload.

searchDocs.title: Protecting _fegg/​
searchDocs.content: htdocs/_fegg/ is inside the document root in the standard layout. It is protected by .htaccess files, and every PHP file starts with defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit;. Check a live site with ./fegg-cli doctor https://example.com after every FTP upload: it also warns about outdated .htaccess rules. See Directory structure and fegg-cli.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public void Application::setHtmlHeader( string $header )   Sends an HTTP response header (it calls PHP's header()). Call it before the page is output, for example before Application::displayPage.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$header	string Header line, such as Content-Type: application/json

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $this->setHtmlHeader('Content-Type: text/javascript; charset=UTF-8'); echo $this->fetchPage('data/config_js');   Sends the Content-Type: text/javascript; charset=UTF-8 header, then outputs the template.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public void Application::setHidden( mixed $name, [ mixed $value = "" ] ) public void Application::unsetHidden( string $name )   setHidden() stores a value that the {{ hidden }} tag prints as <input type="hidden">. unsetHidden() removes one again.  Names and values are HTML-escaped (a value that is already escaped is not escaped twice). An array value is printed as one input per element, with names such as tags[0] and tags[1].  See also Hidden.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$name	string / array Hidden name, or an array name => value to set several at once $value	string / array	""	Hidden value (ignored when $name is an array)

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $this->setHidden('internal_id', $internalId);   Template {{ hidden }}   Output <input type="hidden" name="internal_id" value="12">

searchDocs.title: Assigning multiple values​
searchDocs.content: Controller $this->setHidden(array( 'foo' => 'bar', 'tags' => array('a', 'b'), ));   Template {{ hidden }}   Output <input type="hidden" name="foo" value="bar"><input type="hidden" name="tags[0]" value="a"><input type="hidden" name="tags[1]" value="b">

searchDocs.title: Removing a value​
searchDocs.content: Controller $this->unsetHidden('internal_id');

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public void Application::setSiteinfo( string $id, mixed $value )   Sets one entry of the site information. Templates read it as $site (set by Application::fetchPage).  The base controller (Fegg\Controller\Controller::__init()) already loads every entry of htdocs/_fegg/site/config/site_info.php this way, so $site.title, $site.description … have their default values on every page. Call setSiteinfo() in a controller to change a value for one page. A template can also change it with {{ assign }} before its {{ transclude }} (see Assign).

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$id	string Key $value	mixed Value (a string or an array)

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: htdocs/_fegg/site/config/site_info.php $site_info = array( 'title' => 'Example Inc.', 'description' => '', // ... );   Controller $this->setSiteinfo('title', 'News | Example Inc.');   Template <title>{{ $site.title }}</title>   Output <title>News | Example Inc.</title>

searchDocs.title: template:lint​
searchDocs.content: ./fegg-cli template:lint # every template in site/template and core/template ./fegg-cli template:lint path/to/file.tpl ... # only the given files   The command compiles the templates without running them and prints one line per problem, as file:line: message, using the line of the .tpl file. It ends with OK: n template(s), or with NG: n problem(s) in m template(s) and exit status 1, so it can be used in CI. A file given on the command line must be under a template directory.  Run it after every template change. composer test runs it too, on every template of the repository.  Example output htdocs/_fegg/site/template/news/detail.tpl:2: text outside {{ section }} in a template with {{ transclude }}: it is output before the parent template htdocs/_fegg/site/template/news/detail.tpl:6: unknown tag {{ endif }} (it is output as text) htdocs/_fegg/site/template/news/detail.tpl:8: include target not found: ./missing htdocs/_fegg/site/template/news/detail.tpl:9: unknown modifier "fegDate" (define it in site/functions/*.php) NG: 4 problem(s) in 1 template(s)

searchDocs.title: What it checks​
searchDocs.content: Check	Example messageTags no rule understands. They would be output as text	unknown tag {{ endif }} (it is output as text) Unclosed blocks (if, foreach, loop, section)	{{ foreach }} is never closed Extra closing tags, else outside an if	{{ end }} without an open block, {{ else }} outside an {{ if }} A closing tag that does not match its block (it still closes the open block)	{{ end foreach }} closes the {{ if }} opened on line 1 PHP that does not parse after compiling (a broken expression in if, assign, code …)	compiled PHP does not parse: syntax error, ... Missing transclude parent	transclude target "/no/such/frame" not found Missing include, include head, include foot and include html targets (literal paths only)	include target not found: ./missing Modifiers that are not defined PHP functions	unknown modifier "fegDate" (define it in site/functions/*.php) Text outside {{ section }} in a template that uses transclude	text outside {{ section }} in a template with {{ transclude }}: ... An output in <script> without feggJs and noescape	... is in <script>: write {{ $value|feggJs|noescape }} (no quotes around it) An output in an on... attribute without feggJs, or with noescape	... is in an event attribute: write {{ $value|feggJs }} (no quotes around it, no noescape) An output starting an href, src, action or formaction value without feggUrl	... starts a URL: write {{ $value|feggUrl }} so javascript: URLs are refused  The last three checks skip $site values (configuration), the CMS URL modifiers (getImageUrl, getImageUrlFromDB, getFileUrl, getFileRawUrl) for URLs, and <script> elements whose type is not JavaScript (such as text/template). See Security.

searchDocs.title: TemplateException​
searchDocs.content: These problems throw Fegg\Template\TemplateException:  the template given to displayPage() / fetchPage() / displayTemplate() / fetchTemplate() does not exist;an {{ include }} target or the {{ transclude }} parent does not exist;blocks are unbalanced (an unclosed block, an extra {{ end }}, an {{ else }} outside an {{ if }});the cache file cannot be written (check that htdocs/_fegg/site/data/cache/template/ is writable).  Uncaught, the exception becomes an HTTP 500 and is written to the PHP error log. Nothing of the half-rendered page is sent. The message names the template and the line, for example {{ if }} is never closed (htdocs/_fegg/site/template/news/detail.tpl:4).  Catch it when a missing template is a normal case:  try { $this->displayPage('campaign/current'); } catch (\Fegg\Template\TemplateException $e) { $this->displayPage('not_found'); }

searchDocs.title: Errors inside a template​
searchDocs.content: A template runs as PHP compiled into the cache (htdocs/_fegg/site/data/cache/template/*.cache.php). The compiled code keeps the line numbers of the .tpl file, and Fegg maps errors back to the template: the error log gets a Template: <file>.tpl:<line> line.  PHP error log Fegg: Uncaught ErrorException: Undefined array key "x" in /path/to/htdocs/_fegg/site/data/cache/template/@news@detail.1a2b3c4d.cache.php:12 Template: htdocs/_fegg/site/template/news/detail.tpl:12 Stack trace: ...   In developer mode (a developer_ip address on a server whose FEGG_ENV is not production) the browser also shows the error, the Template: line and the stack trace. Everyone else gets the error page (see Logging and errors).

searchDocs.title: Pitfalls​
searchDocs.content: Closing tags: {{ endif }}, {{ /if }} and {{ endforeach }} are not tags; they are output as text. Use {{ end }} (any block), {{ end foreach }} or {{ end section name }}.Inside {{ section }}, {{ assign }}, {{ include head }} and {{ include foot }} only affect the section, because it runs as a function. Write them at the top level of the template.Text outside sections: in a template that uses {{ transclude }}, everything outside {{ section }} blocks is output before the parent layout.Loop variables share the namespace of $page, $site …: {{ foreach $list as $page }} overwrites $page.Concatenation: in tags, $a.b is always array access. Write $a . $b, with spaces, to concatenate.Arrays need a modifier: {{ $array }} outputs nothing; {{ $array|feggImplode:', ' }} or {{ $array|feggJs|noescape }} turns it into text.Defaults for unset values: {{ $missing|feggDefault:'-' }} outputs nothing, because output is skipped for unset values before the modifier runs. Use {{ if $x }}...{{ else }}-{{ end }}.Null-safe only in some places: an unset variable reads as null in if, else if, assign and loop. In modifier arguments and {{ code }}, it raises a warning on PHP 8, which Fegg turns into an error.Relative paths: a path without / in include / transclude is relative to the template that contains the tag. Counting ../ is the classic mistake: prefer /-rooted paths.Literal braces: text that contains {{ (Vue templates, copied text) is read as a tag. Write {-{ and }-} (see Literal braces).

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public string Application::fetchPage( string $template )   Collects the standard template variables (below), renders the template with Application::fetchTemplate and returns the result instead of outputting it. Application::displayPage uses it.  Use it when you need the page as a string: to post-process it, or as the body of a mail. Unlike displayPage(), it does not end the response. The security headers do not depend on which method you use (see Security).

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$template	string Template name relative to the template root, without .tpl

searchDocs.title: Template variables​
searchDocs.content: Variable	Content$page	$this->page of the controller: the page data $site	Site information: site/config/site_info.php (loaded by the base controller) plus values set with setSiteinfo $in	Request parameters, $_GET and $_POST ($this->in()). Not escaped: always output them with the default escaping $config	Loaded config files ($this->config) $session	Session data, plus session_id and session_name while a session is active. Reading it does not start a session: without a session cookie it is empty $cookie	Cookie data $className	Controller class name without namespace (News) $languageCode	Current language code $define	User-defined PHP constants $hiddenForTemplate	Values set with setHidden, printed by the {{ hidden }} tag

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/Foo.php <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; class Foo extends Controller { // URL: https://example.com/foo/bar/?get=param public function bar() { $this->page['baz'] = 'qux'; echo $this->fetchPage('foo/bar'); } }   htdocs/_fegg/site/template/foo/bar.tpl Baz param : {{ $page.baz }} $_GET[get] param : {{ $in.get }} Controller name : {{ $className }}   Output Baz param : qux $_GET[get] param : param Controller name : Foo   note The site-wide Basic authentication (basic_auth_scope = 1) is checked before the controller runs, so it also protects actions that only call fetchPage().

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public void Application::displayPage( string $template )   Renders the template with Application::fetchPage (so $page, $site, $in … are available), outputs the page and ends the response by throwing Fegg\Http\Halt (not exit; see Ending a response). Code after displayPage() does not run. A catch (\Throwable $e) around it must rethrow Fegg\Http\Halt.  The security headers (X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy ...) are sent for every response before the controller runs, not by displayPage() (see Security). To let other sites show one page in a frame, call $this->allowFraming() before displayPage().  This is the method to use for every page. The site-wide Basic authentication (basic_auth_scope = 1) is checked earlier, before the controller runs.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$template	string Template name relative to the template root, without .tpl (news/detail)

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/News.php <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; class News extends Controller { public function detail($id = '') { $this->page['title'] = 'Hello'; $this->displayPage('news/detail'); } }   htdocs/_fegg/site/template/news/detail.tpl <h1>{{ $page.title }}</h1>   Output <h1>Hello</h1>

searchDocs.title: Errors​
searchDocs.content: When the template does not exist, Fegg\Template\TemplateException is thrown. Uncaught, it becomes an HTTP 500 that is written to the PHP error log; nothing of the half-rendered page is sent. Catch it when a missing template is expected:  try { $this->displayPage('campaign/current'); } catch (\Fegg\Template\TemplateException $e) { $this->displayPage('not_found'); }   warning Never build the template name from user input without checking it. A controller that chooses a template from its URL arguments should only be reachable through site/config/route.php (implement Fegg\Http\RouteOnly, like the skeleton's Site\Controller\Page).

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public void Application::displayTemplate( string $template, [ array $assignedValue = array() ] )   Finds the template (site/template/ first, then core/template/), compiles it when the cache is missing or out of date, and outputs it. Only the variables in $assignedValue are available: $page, $site, $in … are not set. Use Application::displayPage for pages.  The template engine itself uses this method for {{ include }} and {{ transclude }}. Inside a template, a name not starting with / is relative to the directory of the current template; from a controller, names are relative to the template root.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$template	string Template name without .tpl (foo/bar) $assignedValue	array	array()	Variables for the template: the key title becomes $title

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/Foo.php <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; class Foo extends Controller { public function bar() { $this->displayTemplate('foo/bar', array( 'title' => 'Hello', 'items' => array('a', 'b'), )); } }   htdocs/_fegg/site/template/foo/bar.tpl <h1>{{ $title }}</h1> {{ foreach $items as $item }}<p>{{ $item }}</p>{{ end foreach }} {{ if $page.baz }}not shown: $page is not set{{ end }}   Output <h1>Hello</h1> <p>a</p><p>b</p>   note Do not include the .tpl extension in the name. A missing template throws Fegg\Template\TemplateException (see Lint and errors).

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public string Application::fetchTemplate( string $template, [ array $assignedValue = array() ] )   Same as Application::displayTemplate, but returns the output as a string instead of printing it. Leading blank lines are removed from the result.  The name is always relative to the template root, even when fetchTemplate is called while another template is running. If rendering fails, the partial output is discarded and the exception is thrown again.  Typical uses are mail bodies and HTML fragments for Ajax responses.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$template	string Template name without .tpl $assignedValue	array	array()	Variables for the template: the key name becomes $name

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $body = $this->fetchTemplate('mail/notice', array( 'name' => $this->in('name'), ));   htdocs/_fegg/site/template/mail/notice.tpl A message from {{ $name }}.   note Do not include the .tpl extension in the name. $page, $site, $in … are only set by Application::fetchPage: pass what the template needs in $assignedValue.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: {{ assign $var = expression }} {{ assign $var.key = expression }}   Sets a template variable to the value of a PHP expression. The expression may use template variables ($page.title), string literals, operators and PHP functions, but cannot contain }. Nothing is output.  A variable that is not set reads as null in the expression, without a warning.  A common use is to change site information ($site) before {{ transclude }}, so that the parent layout sees the new value.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: htdocs/_fegg/site/template/about.tpl {{ assign $site.title = 'About | ' . $site.title }} {{ transclude '/template/siteframe' }} {{ section contents }} {{ assign $format = 'Y/m/d' }} <p>{{ $page.updated|feggDate:$format }}</p> {{ end section contents }}   htdocs/_fegg/site/template/template/siteframe.tpl <title>{{ $site.title }}</title>   Output <title>About | Example Inc.</title>   note Inside a {{ section }}, assign only changes the variable for that section: a section runs as a function. To change a value the layout reads (such as $site.title), assign it at the top level of the template, outside every section.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: {{ call 'controller/method' }}   Creates a new instance of a controller and runs one of its methods at this place. Whatever the method prints is part of the page.  The path is written in single quotes. The first segments name the controller, like a URL: news is Site\Controller\News, cms/news is Site\Controller\Cms\News (then Fegg\Controller\... of the core).The next segment is the method; without it, index() is called.Further segments are ignored: the method is called without arguments.The controller is resolved when the template is compiled. When no controller matches, the tag is left in the page as text and fegg-cli template:lint reports it as an unknown tag.Only the constructor runs before the method, not __init(). Have the method print a fragment (for example echo $this->fetchTemplate(...)). Do not call displayPage(): it ends the request.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: htdocs/_fegg/site/controller/Banner.php <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; class Banner extends Controller { public function latest() { echo $this->fetchTemplate('parts/banner', array( 'text' => 'Campaign now on', )); } }   htdocs/_fegg/site/template/parts/banner.tpl <p class="c-banner">{{ $text }}</p>   Template {{ call 'banner/latest' }}   Output <p class="c-banner">Campaign now on</p>   tip To share a piece of HTML, {{ include }} is simpler. Load data in the page's own controller when you can, and keep {{ call }} for fragments that need their own controller code.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: {{ code statement }}   Runs PHP statements in the template. Nothing is output unless the statement itself prints something.  Template variables are written as usual ($page.data, $categories). A variable assigned in {{ code }} can be used by the following tags.Several statements can be separated with ;. The code cannot contain { or }, so blocks such as if (...) { } are not possible: use {{ if }} and {{ foreach }} instead.Unlike {{ if }} and {{ assign }}, the code is not null-safe: on PHP 8, reading a variable that is not set raises a warning, which Fegg's error handler turns into an exception (HTTP 500).  Keep logic in the controller. {{ code }} is for small things such as calling a helper function; for a value, prefer {{ assign }}.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Template {{ code $categories = feggCategories('news') }} <select name="category"> {{ foreach $categories as $key => $label }} <option value="{{ $key }}"{{ selected key=$key value=$in.category }}>{{ $label }}</option> {{ end foreach }} </select>   feggCategories() returns the list news of site/config/category_info.php.  Template <a href="{{ $site.prefix }}?p={{ $page.pager.next_page }}&{{ code echoSearchQuery() }}">Next</a>   echoSearchQuery() prints the current request parameters (without p) as a query string.  warning Templates are code: {{ code }} runs any PHP. Only developers may edit templates. See Security.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: {{ checked key=$optionValue value=$currentValue }} {{ selected key=$optionValue value=$currentValue }} {{ checked key=1 value=$currentValue typecheck=true }}   Prints checked (or selected, with a leading space) when the current value matches the value of this input or option:  key is the value of this <input> / <option>: a variable, a number or a quoted string.value is the current value, usually from the request ($in.category) or the stored data ($page.data[$id]).It matches when value == key, or when value is an array that contains key (multiple checkboxes, multiple select).Add typecheck=true to compare with === (and a strict in_array).Nothing is printed when value is not set.  Put the tag directly after the other attributes, without a space before it: the output starts with its own space.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $this->page['current'] = 'value';   Template <label><input type="radio" name="radio" value="value"{{ checked key='value' value=$page.current }}> value</label> <label><input type="radio" name="radio" value="other"{{ checked key='other' value=$page.current }}> other</label> <select name="select"> <option value="value"{{ selected key='value' value=$page.current }}>value</option> <option value="other"{{ selected key='other' value=$page.current }}>other</option> </select>   Output <label><input type="radio" name="radio" value="value" checked> value</label> <label><input type="radio" name="radio" value="other"> other</label> <select name="select"> <option value="value" selected>value</option> <option value="other">other</option> </select>

searchDocs.title: Multiple checkboxes​
searchDocs.content: Controller $this->page['data']['colors'] = array('red', 'blue'); $this->page['colors'] = array('red', 'green', 'blue');   Template {{ foreach $page.colors as $color }} <label><input type="checkbox" name="colors[]" value="{{ $color }}"{{ checked key=$color value=$page.data.colors }}> {{ $color }}</label> {{ end foreach }}   Output <label><input type="checkbox" name="colors[]" value="red" checked> red</label> <label><input type="checkbox" name="colors[]" value="green"> green</label> <label><input type="checkbox" name="colors[]" value="blue" checked> blue</label>   See Options to build all the <option> tags of a <select> from an array.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: {{* comment *}}   Everything between {{* and *}} is removed when the template is compiled: it never reaches the browser, unlike an HTML comment. A comment may span several lines, and tags inside it are ignored, so it can also disable a part of the template.  The newlines of a comment are kept, so errors and fegg-cli template:lint still report the right .tpl line after a multi-line comment.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Template <p>Visible</p> {{* TODO: show the campaign banner from April *}} {{* {{ if $page.campaign }} <p>{{ $page.campaign.title }}</p> {{ end }} *}} <p>Also visible</p>   Output <p>Visible</p> <p>Also visible</p>   The lines of the comments remain as empty lines.  note <!-- ... --> is an ordinary HTML comment: it is sent to the browser, and the tags inside it still run.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: {{ hidden }}   Prints an <input type="hidden"> for every value set with $this->setHidden() in the controller. Names and values are HTML-escaped. Array values become one input per element (tags[0], tags[1] …).  Put it inside the <form>. It is typically used to carry an ID or a one-time ticket from the input screen to the confirmation and save steps.  See also Application::setHidden.

searchDocs.title: How to use modifiers​
searchDocs.content: A modifier follows the variable after a pipe (|). Arguments follow the modifier name after colons (:). Modifiers can be chained: they are applied from left to right, each one receiving the result of the previous one.  {{ $page.post_date|feggDate:'Y/m/d' }} {{ $page.text|lineStrimWidth:80|br }}   Any PHP function works as a modifier: {{ $x|name:arg1:arg2 }} calls name($x, arg1, arg2).Arguments are PHP expressions: quote strings ('Y/m/d'), and use template variables freely (feggDate:$format). A : or | inside a quoted string is part of the string.The result is HTML-escaped like any output, unless noescape is in the chain.Modifiers only run when the variable is set: {{ $missing|feggDefault:'-' }} outputs nothing, so use {{ if }} for defaults. Arrays are passed to modifiers ({{ $tags|feggImplode:', ' }}); when the result is still an array, nothing is output.An unknown modifier is reported by fegg-cli template:lint (see Lint and errors).

searchDocs.title: noescape​
searchDocs.content: Outputs the value without HTML escaping. Use it only for trusted HTML (CMS rich text written by administrators, messages from your own config). See Security.  Controller $this->page['foo'] = '<p>bar</p>';   Template {{ $page.foo }} {{ $page.foo|noescape }}   Output &lt;p&gt;bar&lt;/p&gt; <p>bar</p>

searchDocs.title: br​
searchDocs.content: Escapes the value, then converts newlines to <br /> (nl2br).  Controller $this->page['foo'] = "First line.\nSecond line.";   Template {{ $page.foo|br }}   Output First line.<br /> Second line.

searchDocs.title: replace​
searchDocs.content: replace:'pattern':'replacement' replaces with mb_ereg_replace(). The pattern is a regular expression, so escape special characters ('\.').  Template {{ $page.tel|replace:'-':'' }}

searchDocs.title: Fegg modifiers​
searchDocs.content: Defined in htdocs/_fegg/core/functions/modifier.php.  Modifier	DescriptionfeggDate:'Y/m/d'	Formats a date string or a Unix timestamp with the date() format. Also accepts x / X (Japanese day of the week: 火 / 火曜日) and V / v (Japanese era and year: 令和 / 7). Outputs nothing for an empty or invalid date feggImplode:', '	Joins an array with the glue feggDefault:'-'	The replacement when the value is an empty string or an empty array. Does not apply to unset variables feggCheck:'value':'yes':'no'	'yes' when the value is identical (===) to 'value', otherwise 'no' feggReplace:'a':'b'	str_replace('a', 'b', $value) feggPregReplace:'/a/':'b'	preg_replace('/a/', 'b', $value). An optional third argument is the maximum number of replacements feggUrlParam:$params	Appends query parameters (an array or a string) to a URL, with ? or & feggUrl	A URL safe for href / src: any scheme other than http, https, mailto and tel (javascript:, data: …) becomes # feggJs	The value as a JavaScript literal (string, number, array, object, null) with <, >, &, ' and " encoded. Do not put quotes around it. See Security  Controller $this->page['post_date'] = '2025-04-01 10:00:00'; $this->page['category'] = '1'; $this->page['data']['link'] = 'javascript:alert(1)'; $this->page['query'] = array('category' => 2, 'p' => 3); $this->setSiteinfo('prefix', '/news/');   Template {{ $page.post_date|feggDate:'Y年n月j日(x)' }} <li class="c-tab{{ $page.category|feggCheck:'1':' is-active':'' }}"> <a href="{{ $page.data.link|feggUrl }}">Link</a> <a href="{{ $site.prefix|feggUrlParam:$page.query }}">Search</a>   Output 2025年4月1日(火) <li class="c-tab is-active"> <a href="#">Link</a> <a href="/news/?category=2&amp;p=3">Search</a>

searchDocs.title: Joining an array​
searchDocs.content: Template {{ $page.tags|feggImplode:', ' }}

searchDocs.title: CMS modifiers​
searchDocs.content: Defined in htdocs/_fegg/core/functions/cms-modifier.php and model.php.  Modifier	DescriptiongetImageUrl	URL of a CMS image from its ID getImageUrl:320	Resized to a width of 320px getImageUrl:780:360	Resized to 780 × 360px. A third argument changes the crop mode in the file name (default 'i') getImageUrlFromDB, getImageUrlFromDB:320, getImageUrlFromDB:780:360	URL that generates the image on every request (/cms/image/get/...) getFileUrl	URL of a CMS file from its ID getFileRawUrl	Direct URL of the stored file (looks the file up in cms_file) byteConvert	A byte count as a readable size: 1536 → 1.5 KB lineStrimWidth:40	Removes tags and newlines, then shortens the text to a display width of 40, adding …. A second argument replaces … url2link	Turns URLs in text into <a> links.
