searchDocs.content: public array|null Model::id( mixed $id )   Returns the row whose primary key (see setPrimary) is $id, or null when there is none. A public model ($is_admin = false) also returns null for a row that is not visible, and deleted rows (valid = 0) are never returned. Conditions chained before it with where also apply.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$id	mixed Target primary ID

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $record = $model->id($this->in('id')); if ($record === null) { // 404 }

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public string Model::insert( string $item, array $data )   Inserts one row and returns the new ID as a string. For new code, use insertRow: insert() writes '' for every column listed in $item that is missing from $data, and cannot store NULL.  $data is an associative array (values matched to $item by name) or a list (values in the order of $item). created, modified and valid are filled automatically and bind types are applied.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$item	string Columns, separated by commas $data	array Values

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $item = 'title, content'; $data = array( 'title' => 'Sample title', 'content' => 'Sample content', ); // Returns the new ID $insertedId = $model->insert($item, $data); // -> '24'

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public int|string Model::insertRow( array $row )   Inserts one row from column => value pairs and returns the new ID (an int for integer keys).  Only the given columns are written; null is stored as NULL.created, modified and valid are filled automatically. Give them only to override them.bind types are applied.Throws InvalidArgumentException for an empty array, a column name that is not a plain name, or a value that is an array or an object. A failed insert (for example a duplicate key) throws Fegg\Database\QueryException.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$row	array Values (column => value)

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $id = $model->insertRow(array( 'title' => $this->in('title'), 'category' => 2, 'post_date' => '2026-01-15 10:00:00', 'image_id' => null, )); // -> 24

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public array Model::insertRows( array $rows )   Inserts each row with insertRow inside one transaction and returns the new IDs in order. When one row fails, none is inserted and the exception is rethrown. Throws InvalidArgumentException when an element of $rows is not an array.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$rows	array List of rows (column => value arrays)

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $ids = $model->insertRows(array( array('title' => 'First', 'category' => 1), array('title' => 'Second', 'category' => 2), )); // -> array(25, 26)

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public int Model::increment( string $column, mixed $id, [ int|float $by = 1 ] )   Adds $by to $column of the row whose primary key is $id, in the UPDATE itself ("column" = "column" + ?), and returns the number of updated rows. Simultaneous requests do not lose counts, as they would when reading, adding and writing back.  Like every update, it also sets modified. Call unsetRegularUseQuery first to leave modified alone (for example for a view counter).  Throws InvalidArgumentException when $column is not a plain name or $by is not a number.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$column	string Numeric column $id	mixed Target primary ID $by	int/float	1	Amount to add; negative to subtract

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller // The table has a view_count INTEGER column $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // Update "cms_news" Set "view_count" = "view_count" + 1 Where news_id = 24 $model->unsetRegularUseQuery()->increment('view_count', 24); // Subtract 2 (modified is updated) $model->increment('view_count', 24, -2);

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Model::join( string|array $table, [ string $type = 'INNER', string $on = null, mixed $data = [] ] )   Joins another table. $table is a table name, or array('table', 'alias'); both must be plain names, or InvalidArgumentException is thrown. $on takes ? placeholders and $data works as in where.  The automatic valid = 1 and visible conditions only apply to the model's own table. Add them to $on for the joined table when you need them.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$table	string/array Table name, or array('table', 'alias') $type	string	'INNER'	'INNER', 'LEFT' or 'RIGHT' (anything else: INNER) $on	string	null	ON condition with ? placeholders $data	mixed	[]	Values for the ON placeholders

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // Select cms_news.*, f.org_name // From "cms_news" // LEFT JOIN "cms_file" AS "f" ON f.file_id = cms_news.file_id AND f.valid = 1 // Where ... $records = $model ->select('cms_news.*, f.org_name') ->join(array('cms_file', 'f'), 'LEFT', 'f.file_id = cms_news.file_id AND f.valid = ?', 1) ->find();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Model::listMax( [ int $listMax = 10 ] )   Sets the number of rows per page of find. Without it, find() returns 10 rows. A value under 1 is treated as 1. Only find() uses it: use limit with all instead of a large listMax() to get every row.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$listMax	int	10	Rows per page

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // First page, 5 rows $records = $model->listMax(5)->find();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public array|null Model::one( [ array $options = [] ] )   Returns the first matching row as an associative array, or null when nothing matches. order decides which row is first; the offset of limit is used.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$options	array	[]	array('select' => ...) overrides select

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // The newest news, or null $latest = $model->order('post_date', 'desc')->one(); $record = $model->where('title = ?', $title)->one(); if ($record === null) { // not found }

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Model::limit( int $count, [ int $offset = 0 ] )   Adds LIMIT to all, column and toSql; one, value and exists use the offset. count ignores it. find pages with listMax and current instead and throws LogicException when limit() was set.  Throws InvalidArgumentException when $count is under 1 or $offset under 0.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$count	int Maximum number of rows $offset	int	0	Number of rows to skip

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // The 5 newest $records = $model->order('post_date', 'desc')->limit(5)->all(); // The next 5 (rows 6 to 10) $records = $model->order('post_date', 'desc')->limit(5, 5)->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Model::orderRaw( string $expression )   Adds an ORDER BY expression as it is. Use it for what order does not accept: CASE, functions, several keys in one string. The expression is written into the SQL unchanged: never put user input in it.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$expression	string ORDER BY expression

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // Category 1 first, then the newest // ... Order By CASE WHEN category = 1 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, post_date DESC $records = $model->orderRaw('CASE WHEN category = 1 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, post_date DESC')->find();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Model::order( string $order, [ string $duration = 'ASC' ] )   Adds a column to ORDER BY. Call it again for a second sort key.  $order must be a column name (post_date or cms_news.post_date); anything else, such as 'post_date desc' or an expression, throws InvalidArgumentException. Use orderRaw for expressions.$duration is DESC (case-insensitive) or anything else for ASC, so it is safe to pass a sort direction from the request.order('random') sorts in random order (ORDER BY RANDOM(), an SQLite function).

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$order	string Column name, or 'random' $duration	string	'ASC'	'ASC' or 'DESC'

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // ... Order By post_date DESC,news_id DESC $records = $model->order('post_date', 'desc')->order('news_id', 'desc')->find(); // 3 random news $records = $model->order('random')->limit(3)->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public array Model::pragma( string $mode )   Runs an SQLite PRAGMA on the model's table and returns its rows. SQLite only.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$mode	string Pragma mode

searchDocs.title: Pragma mode​
searchDocs.content: Mode	Querytable	PRAGMA table_info("table") (also any unknown mode) index_list	PRAGMA index_list("table") index	PRAGMA index_info("table")

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', )); // PRAGMA table_info("cms_news") $columns = $model->pragma('table'); print_r($columns[0]);   Output Array ( [cid] => 0 [name] => news_id [type] => INTEGER [notnull] => 1 [dflt_value] => [pk] => 1 )

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Model::reset()   Forgets the conditions set with the chain methods: where, having, order, join, group, select, listMax, current and limit. The model does this by itself after every query, failed ones included, so call it only to drop a chain you built but did not run. The table, primary key, visible flag, bind types and the pager are kept.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', )); $model->where('category = ?', 1)->order('post_date', 'desc'); // Changed our mind: start again $model->reset(); // Select * From "cms_news" Where 1 = 1 And "cms_news".valid = 1 $records = $model->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Model::select( string $select )   Sets the columns of the next SELECT (default *). The text is written into the SQL as it is: never put user input in it. Like every chain method, it is reset after the query.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$select	string Columns or expressions, separated by commas

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // Get the `news_id` and `title` columns $records = $model->select('news_id, title')->find(); // Expressions work too $records = $model->select('category, count(*) AS n')->group('category')->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Model::setBindParam( array $bind )   Replaces every bind type set before. See addBindParam for the types and what they do.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$bind	array Bind types (column => type)

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(); $model->setBindParam(array( 'category' => 'INTEGER', 'image_id' => 'INTEGER', 'file_id' => 'INTEGER', 'post_date' => 'DATETIME', )); // Same as the following $model = new Model(false, array( 'bind' => array( 'category' => 'INTEGER', 'image_id' => 'INTEGER', 'file_id' => 'INTEGER', 'post_date' => 'DATETIME', ), ));

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Model::setPrimary( string $id )   The primary key is used by id, updateRow, delete, erase and the other methods that take an ID. Throws InvalidArgumentException when $id is not a plain name.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$id	string Primary key column name

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(); $model->setPrimary('news_id'); // Same as the following $model = new Model(false, array( 'id' => 'news_id', ));

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public string Model::toSql()   Returns the SELECT that all would run with the conditions set so far, with the values filled in, without running it. Like after a query, the conditions are cleared afterwards. The values are quoted for reading only: never run the result.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); echo $model ->where('category = ?', 2) ->whereIn('news_id', array(1, 2)) ->order('post_date', 'desc') ->limit(5) ->toSql();   Output Select * From "cms_news" Where category = 2 AND news_id IN (1, 2) AND cms_news.visible = '1' And "cms_news".valid = 1 Order By post_date DESC Limit 0, 5

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public mixed Model::transaction( callable $callback )   Runs $callback in a transaction and returns what it returns. The transaction is committed when the callback returns and rolled back when it throws; the exception is then rethrown.  The callback receives this model.Every query inside the callback takes part, whatever model (or Fegg\Database\Pdo) runs it.A transaction() call inside another one joins the outer transaction.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$callback	callable Receives this model

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Model; $news = new Model(true, array('table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible')); $labs = new Model(true, array('table' => 'cms_lab', 'id' => 'lab_id', 'visible' => 'visible')); $id = $news->transaction(function (Model $news) use ($labs) { $id = $news->insertRow(array('title' => 'A')); $labs->insertRow(array('title' => 'B')); // another model joins the same transaction return $id; });

searchDocs.content: public int Model::updateRowsWhere( array $row, string $where, [ mixed $params = [] ] )   Updates every row matching $where and returns the number of updated rows. Columns are written as in updateRow. $params works as in where: one value, or an array of values in placeholder order (an array on a single IN (?) placeholder expands it).  The condition is required: an empty $where throws InvalidArgumentException. Pass '1 = 1' to really update every row. Conditions chained with where are not used.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$row	array Values (column => value) $where	string Condition with ? placeholders $params	mixed	[]	One value, or an array of values in placeholder order

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(true, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // Hide every news of category 3 $updated = $model->updateRowsWhere(array('visible' => 0), 'category = ?', 3); $updated = $model->updateRowsWhere(array('category' => 1), 'news_id IN (?)', array(4, 5, 6)); // Every row $updated = $model->updateRowsWhere(array('visible' => 1), '1 = 1');

searchDocs.content: public int Model::updateWhere( string $item, array $data, string $where, mixed $wh_data )   Updates every row matching $where and returns the number of updated rows. For new code, use updateRowsWhere: updateWhere() writes '' for every column listed in $item that is missing from $data, and cannot store NULL.  $wh_data is one value, or an array with one value per placeholder. The condition is required: an empty $where throws InvalidArgumentException (Fegg 4 updated every row). Pass '1 = 1' to really update every row.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$item	string Columns, separated by commas $data	array Values $where	string Condition with ? placeholders $wh_data	mixed Values for the placeholders

AND news_id > ?', array(2, 10));

searchDocs.title: Arguments​

Where post_date BETWEEN '2026-01-01 00:00:00' AND '2026-01-31 23:59:59' AND ... $records = $model->whereBetween('post_date', '2026-01-01 00:00:00', '2026-01-31 23:59:59')->find();

searchDocs.content: public self Model::whereClose()   Closes the bracket opened with whereOpen.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $model->where('category = ?', 2); $model->whereOpen(); $model->where('title = ?', 'foo'); $model->where('post_date <= ?', '2021-01-01', 'OR'); $model->whereClose(); // Select * // From "cms_news" // Where category = 2 // AND (title = 'foo' OR post_date <= '2021-01-01') // AND cms_news.visible = '1' And "cms_news".valid = 1 $records = $model->find();

searchDocs.content: public self Model::whereIn( string $column, array $values, [ string $andOr = 'AND' ] )   Adds column IN (?, ?, ...). An empty array matches no row (1 = 0), so an empty selection returns nothing instead of failing. Throws InvalidArgumentException when $column is not a plain name.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$column	string Column name (news_id or cms_news.news_id) $values	array Values to match $andOr	string	'AND'	How it joins the previous condition: AND or OR

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // ... Where news_id IN (1, 2, 3) AND ... $records = $model->whereIn('news_id', array(1, 2, 3))->all(); // ... Where 1 = 0 AND ... (no rows) $records = $model->whereIn('news_id', array())->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Model::where( string $query, [ mixed $data = [], string $andOr = 'AND' ] )   Adds a condition with ? placeholders. Values are always bound, never written into the SQL. Several calls are joined with AND (or OR with $andOr).  $data is one value, or an array of values in placeholder order. A query without placeholders ('note IS NULL') needs none.An array bound to a single placeholder expands it: id = ? and id IN (?) become id IN (?, ?, ...), id <> ? / id != ? / id NOT IN (?) become NOT IN, title LIKE ? becomes (title LIKE ? OR title LIKE ? ...) and title NOT LIKE ? becomes (title NOT LIKE ? AND ...). An empty array matches no row (=, IN, LIKE) or every row (<>, NOT IN, NOT LIKE). An array on any other operator (<, BETWEEN ...) throws InvalidArgumentException when the query runs.A ? inside a quoted string literal ('?') is not a placeholder.An empty $query ('') adds nothing, which is handy for optional search conditions.  A query with its own OR outside brackets is put in brackets when it is joined to other conditions: where('category = ?', 1)->where('title = ? OR summary = ?', array($q, $q)) is category = 1 AND (title = ? OR summary = ?). Fegg 4 wrote category = 1 AND title = ? OR summary = ?, which matched rows of every category. having works the same way.  The conditions the model adds by itself (the visible flag and valid = 1) are joined with AND after yours. When your conditions have an OR outside brackets, the model puts them in brackets first (Where (a = ? OR b = ?) AND ...), so hidden and deleted rows never match. To group conditions inside your own, use whereOpen and whereClose.  For common cases there are helpers that also check the column name: whereIn, whereNotIn, whereLike, whereNull, whereNotNull and whereBetween.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$query	string Condition with ? placeholders (never put user input in it) $data	mixed	[]	One value, or an array of values in placeholder order $andOr	string	'AND'	How it joins the previous condition: AND or OR

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $records = $model->where('category = ?', 2)->find(); // Select * From "cms_news" Where category = 2 AND cms_news.visible = '1' And "cms_news".valid = 1 ... // Several placeholders: an array in placeholder order $records = $model->where('category = ? AND post_date >= ?', array(2, '2026-01-01'))->find(); // An array on one placeholder: IN (...) $records = $model->where('news_id IN (?)', array(1, 2, 3))->find(); // ... Where news_id IN (1, 2, 3) AND ...

searchDocs.title: Complex WHERE query​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $model->where('category = ?', 2); $model->whereOpen(); $model->where('title = ?', 'foo'); $model->where('post_date <= ?', '2021-01-01', 'OR'); $model->whereClose(); // Select * // From "cms_news" // Where category = 2 // AND (title = 'foo' OR post_date <= '2021-01-01') // AND cms_news.visible = '1' And "cms_news".valid = 1 $records = $model->find();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Model::whereNotIn( string $column, array $values, [ string $andOr = 'AND' ] )   Adds column NOT IN (?, ?, ...). An empty array excludes nothing (1 = 1). Throws InvalidArgumentException when $column is not a plain name.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$column	string Column name (news_id or cms_news.news_id) $values	array Values to exclude $andOr	string	'AND'	How it joins the previous condition: AND or OR

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // Other news than the current one // ... Where news_id NOT IN (5) AND ... $records = $model->whereNotIn('news_id', array(5))->order('post_date', 'desc')->limit(3)->all();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public self Model::whereLike( string $column, string $term, [ string $mode = 'contains', string $andOr = 'AND' ] )   Adds column LIKE ? ESCAPE '!'. % and _ in $term match literally, so user input can be passed as it is. Throws InvalidArgumentException when $column is not a plain name or $mode is unknown.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$column	string Column name $term	string Text to search for $mode	string	'contains'	Where the term must be (below) $andOr	string	'AND'	How it joins the previous condition: AND or OR

searchDocs.title: Modes​
searchDocs.content: Mode	Patterncontains	%term% prefix	term% suffix	%term exact	term

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); // ... Where title LIKE '%50!%%' ESCAPE '!' AND ... (titles containing "50%") $records = $model->whereLike('title', '50%')->find(); // Titles starting with "News" $records = $model->whereLike('title', 'News', 'prefix')->find(); // Search title or content $keyword = $this->in('keyword'); $records = $model ->whereOpen() ->whereLike('title', $keyword) ->whereLike('content', $keyword, 'contains', 'OR') ->whereClose() ->find();

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$column	string Column name $andOr	string	'AND'	How it joins the previous condition: AND or OR

searchDocs.title: Example​

searchDocs.content: public self Model::whereOpen( [ string $andOr = 'AND' ] )   Opens a bracket in the WHERE clause; close it with whereClose. The first condition inside the bracket is not prefixed with AND / OR.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$andOr	string	'AND'	How the bracket joins the previous condition: AND or OR

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $model = new Model(false, array( 'table' => 'cms_news', 'id' => 'news_id', 'visible' => 'visible', )); $model->where('category = ?', 2); $model->whereOpen(); $model->where('title = ?', 'foo'); $model->where('post_date <= ?', '2021-01-01', 'OR'); $model->whereClose(); // Select * // From "cms_news" // Where category = 2 // AND (title = 'foo' OR post_date <= '2021-01-01') // AND cms_news.visible = '1' And "cms_news".valid = 1 $records = $model->find();

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: Import Fegg\Tool\OEmbed and create it with new, passing the page URL. The constructor throws an Exception when the URL is not supported or the request fails.  Controller <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Tool\OEmbed; class Movie extends Controller { public function index() { try { $oembed = new OEmbed('https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xxxxxxxxxxx'); $this->page['youtube'] = $oembed->media; } catch (\Exception $e) { $this->page['youtube'] = ''; } $this->displayPage('movie'); } }   Template {{ if $page.youtube }} <iframe width="560" height="315" src="{{ $page.youtube|feggUrl }}" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen class="c-youtube"></iframe> {{ end }}

searchDocs.title: Properties​
searchDocs.content: The result is read through these read-only properties.  Property	Data type	Remarksmedia	string	URL to embed: src of the iframe (video), src of the img (photo) or href of the a (link) type	string	video, photo or link data	array	The whole oEmbed response (title, author_name, thumbnail_url, html ...) service	string	Matched service name in the configuration, e.g. youtube url	string	URL passed to the constructor  Reading any other property throws an Exception.

searchDocs.title: Configuration​
searchDocs.content: The services are defined in htdocs/_fegg/core/config/oembed_schemes.php. Only YouTube is defined by default.  htdocs/_fegg/core/config/oembed_schemes.php <?php defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; $oembed_schemes = array(); $oembed_schemes['youtube'] = array( 'endpoint' => 'https://www.youtube.com/oembed', 'schemes' => array( '|^https?://.*\\.youtube\\.com/watch.*$|i', '|^https?://.*\\.youtube\\.com/v/.*$|i', '|^https?://youtu\\.be/.*$|i', '|^https?://.*\\.youtube\\.com/playlist\\?list\\=.*$|i', '|^https?://youtube\\.com/playlist\\?list\\=.*$|i', ), );   endpoint is the oEmbed endpoint of the service and schemes are regular expressions matching the supported URLs. To add a service, copy the file to htdocs/_fegg/site/config/oembed_schemes.php and add an entry there (the file in site/config/ is used instead of the core's one).

searchDocs.title: Methods​
searchDocs.content: 📄️OEmbed::__construct Get the oEmbed data of a URL

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public OEmbed::__construct( string $url, [ array $config = array() ] )   Finds the service whose schemes match $url, requests its oEmbed endpoint and reads the embedded HTML. The result is available through the properties.  Throws an Exception when no service matches $url, the service has no endpoint, the request fails, or the response has no iframe, img or a element.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$url	string URL of the page to embed $config	array	array()	Options sent to the endpoint (see below)  Key	Data type	Default	Remarksmaxwidth	int	null	Maximum width of the embed maxheight	int	null	Maximum height of the embed

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\OEmbed; $oembed = new OEmbed('https://youtu.be/xxxxxxxxxxx', array('maxwidth' => 640)); echo $oembed->type; // -> "video" echo $oembed->media; // -> "https://www.youtube.com/embed/xxxxxxxxxxx?feature=oembed" echo $oembed->data['title']; // -> Video title

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: Import Fegg\Tool\RSS and create it with new, passing the feed URL.  Controller <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Tool\RSS; class Index extends Controller { public function index() { $rss = new RSS('https://example.com/feed'); $this->page['posts'] = $rss->fetchAll(10); $this->displayPage('index'); } }

searchDocs.title: Entry data​
searchDocs.content: Each entry returned by RSS::fetch and RSS::fetchAll is an array with these keys.  Key	Data type	Remarkstitle	string	Title pubDate	string	Date as written in the feed (pubDate, or dc:date for RSS 1.0) datetime	DateTime	pubDate as a DateTime object link	string	Link URL description	string	Description (HTML entities decoded) content	string	content:encoded (HTML entities decoded) author	string	dc:creator category	array	Category names (category, or dc:subject for RSS 1.0) tag	array	Always an empty array (not implemented)  note Entries whose title contains PR: (advertisements) are skipped.Atom feeds are not supported: no entry is returned.The feed is loaded with simplexml_load_file() in the constructor. A feed that cannot be loaded is not handled, so check the URL beforehand when it may be unavailable.

searchDocs.title: Methods​
searchDocs.content: 📄️RSS::__construct Load RSS feed 📄️RSS::fetch Fetch the next entry of RSS feed 📄️RSS::fetchAll Fetch all entries or specified number of entries of RSS feed

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public RSS::__construct( string $url )   Loads and parses the feed. The entries can then be read with RSS::fetch or RSS::fetchAll.

searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\RSS; $rss = new RSS('https://example.com/feed');

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\RSS; $rss = new RSS('https://example.com/feed'); while ($post = $rss->fetch()) { // $post['title'], $post['link'], $post['datetime'] ... }

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public void Trim::create()   Saves the resized image to the output path given to Trim::setImage. Missing directories are created. JPEG images are saved with quality 90.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Trim; $trim = new Trim(); $trim->setImage('path/to/image.jpg', 'path/to/converted.jpg'); $trim->resizeTrim(300, 300, 'm'); $trim->create();

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: Import Fegg\Tool\Trim and create it with new. Set the source image and the output path with Trim::setImage, resize it with one of the resize* methods, then save it with Trim::create.  Controller <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Tool\Trim; class Thumbnail extends Controller { public function index() { $trim = new Trim(); $trim->setImage('path/to/image.jpg', 'path/to/thumbnail/300_300.jpg'); $trim->resizeTrim(300, 300, 'm'); $trim->create(); // Output the saved image to the browser $trim->view(); } }   The thumbnails of CMS images (Fegg\Controller\Up_dir::image()) are generated with this class.

searchDocs.title: Methods​
searchDocs.content: 📄️Trim::setImage Set target image and output file path 📄️Trim::resize Resize the image to fit in the specified size with keeping ratio 📄️Trim::resizeFill Resize the image with keeping ratio and filling the empty area (Like object-fit: contain) 📄️Trim::resizeForce Resize the image to the specified size ignoring ratio 📄️Trim::resizeTrim Resize the image with keeping ratio and trimming the overflow (Like object-fit: cover) 📄️Trim::create Save the image to the output path 📄️Trim::view Output the saved image to the browser

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public void Trim::resize( int $w, int $h )   The image is scaled down to fit in $w x $h, keeping its aspect ratio. The output may be smaller than $w x $h in one direction. Images smaller than the specified size are not enlarged. 0 means the original width or height.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$w	int Maximum width / 0: original width $h	int Maximum height / 0: original height

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Trim; $trim = new Trim(); $trim->setImage('path/to/image.jpg', 'path/to/converted.jpg'); // Width 300px at most, any height $trim->resize(300, 0); $trim->create();

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public void Trim::resizeFill( int $w, int $h )   The output is exactly $w x $h. The image is scaled down to fit in it, keeping its aspect ratio, and placed in the center. The empty area is white for JPEG output and transparent for PNG output from a PNG source. Images smaller than the specified size are not enlarged. 0 means the original width or height.

searchDocs.title: Other languages​
searchDocs.content: When a language code is passed to the constructor (new Upload('en')), the messages are read from config/en/file_error_message.php (searched in site/config/ first, then core/config/).

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: Import Fegg\Tool\Upload and create it with new. Set the upload directory, then call Upload::upload with the name of the input[type="file"].  Controller <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Tool\Upload; class Entry extends Controller { public function post() { $this->loadConfig('upload_dir'); $upload = new Upload(); $upload->setUploadDir($this->config['upload_dir']['path'] . '/entry'); $upload->setMaxFileSize(5); $upload->setFileType(array('jpg', 'jpeg', 'png', 'pdf')); if ($upload->upload('file', uniqid('f_'), 'Attachment')) { $data = $upload->getUploadedData('file'); // $data['name'], $data['org_name'], $data['type'], $data['size'] ... } else { $errors = $upload->getErrorMessage('file'); } } }   $this->loadConfig('upload_dir') reads site/config/upload_dir.php (path and url of htdocs/up_dir) into $this->config['upload_dir']. The CMS screens (Fegg\Controller\Cms\Image, Media, Multi) use this class in the same way.  Error messages are defined in file_error_message.php, see Configuration.

searchDocs.title: What is checked​
searchDocs.content: The extension must be allowed by setFileType. Script extensions (php, phtml, phar, cgi ...) are refused even when listed.The content must match the extension: getimagesize() for images, the finfo MIME type for known types. A mismatch is the error @content.Files are saved under the name you give (uniqid('f_'), ...), never under the visitor's file name. Keep the original name (org_name) in the database only.Directories are created with mode 0755 and files saved with 0644.

searchDocs.title: Protecting the upload directory​
searchDocs.content: When the upload directory is below the document root, setUploadDir writes an .htaccess into it that denies and disables scripts (.php, .phtml, .phar, .cgi ...), so an uploaded file can never run as code. The CMS dashboard also writes htdocs/up_dir/.htaccess when it opens, and the skeleton ships the file.  fegg-cli doctor and the CMS dashboard report a missing htdocs/up_dir/.htaccess (see fegg-cli). Remember it when you upload over FTP: many FTP clients skip dotfiles. On nginx, .htaccess is ignored: deny scripts under the upload URL yourself.  location ~* ^/up_dir/.*\.(php\d?|phtml|phar|pht|cgi|pl|py|sh)$ { deny all; }

searchDocs.title: Sending stored files​
searchDocs.content: The CMS sends stored files (/up_dir/file/<id>/, the media and image screens) with Fegg\Http\Download::sendHeaders(). It sends X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, a valid Cache-Control, and an RFC 6266 Content-Disposition with the original name escaped (an ASCII fallback plus the UTF-8 name). HTML, SVG, XML and JavaScript files are always sent as attachments, never shown inline. Use it when your own controller sends a stored file:  Controller use Fegg\Http\Download; Download::sendHeaders(array( 'type' => $file['type'], 'size' => filesize($path), 'org_name' => $file['org_name'], ), false); // false: browser cache only (private); true: public $this->halt(file_get_contents($path));

searchDocs.content: public boolean Upload::setFileType( array $type )   Replaces the list of allowed extensions. The extensions are compared in lower case. Returns false when $type is not an array. The default is array('jpg', 'jpeg', 'png', 'gif').  Extensions a web server may run as code (php, php5, phtml, phar, pht, phps, cgi, pl, py, rb, sh, asp, aspx, jsp, shtml, htaccess, htpasswd) are always refused, even when listed here. searchDocs.content: public boolean Upload::setUploadDir( string $dir )   The directory is created (recursively, mode 0755) when it does not exist. Returns true when the directory is writable, otherwise false and the directory is not set.  When the directory is below the document root and has no .htaccess, one is written that stops scripts from running there (see Introduction). An existing .htaccess is left alone.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$dir	string Upload directory

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public boolean Upload::upload( string $name, string $up_name, [ string $label = 'ファイル', boolean $required = true ] )   Checks the file posted as $_FILES[$name] and moves it to {upload directory}/{$up_name}.{extension} with mode 0644. The extension is the lower-cased extension of the original file name.  The checks, in order:  Upload errors and the size (@empty, @size, @failed).The extension must be in setFileType, and must not be a script extension (@type).The content must match the extension (@content): images (jpg, jpeg, png, gif, webp) must be readable by getimagesize(), and for known types (images, pdf, Office files, zip, txt, csv) the MIME type reported by finfo must fit the extension. A PHP file renamed to .jpg, or a text file named .pdf, is refused. Other extensions are checked by the extension only.  Returns true on success. On failure it returns false and the error messages are available with Upload::getErrorMessage. When $required is false and no file was selected, it returns true without saving anything.  Set the upload directory with Upload::setUploadDir before calling this method.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$name	string name attribute of the input[type="file"] $up_name	string File name to save, without extension $label	string	'ファイル'	Item label used in the error messages $required	boolean	true	false: no error when no file is selected

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Tool\Upload; $upload = new Upload(); $upload->setUploadDir($this->config['upload_dir']['path']); if ($upload->upload('image', uniqid('i_'), 'Image')) { $data = $upload->getUploadedData('image'); } else { $errors = $upload->getErrorMessage('image'); } // Optional file $upload->upload('attachment', uniqid('a_'), 'Attachment', false);

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: Import Fegg\Validation and create it with new. Call a check method for each field, then read the result with Validation::getErrorMessage.  Controller <?php namespace Site\Controller; defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; use Fegg\Validation; class Contact extends Controller { public function confirm() { $validation = new Validation(); $id = 'name'; $name = 'お名前'; $validation->required($id, $this->in($id), array('@required', $name)); $validation->maxlength($id, $this->in($id), 50, array('@maxlength', $name, 50)); $id = 'mail'; $name = 'メールアドレス'; $validation->required($id, $this->in($id), array('@required', $name)); $validation->email($id, $this->in($id), array('@email', $name)); $errorMessage = $validation->getErrorMessage(); if (!$errorMessage) { $this->displayPage('contact/confirm'); } else { $this->page['error'] = $errorMessage; $this->displayPage('contact/input'); } } }

searchDocs.title: How checks work​
searchDocs.content: Every check method takes the field name $name first. It is the key of the error message returned by Validation::getErrorMessage.Only the first error of each field is kept: once a field has an error, the next checks of the same field are skipped and return false. Write the checks in order of priority (e.g. required before email).Except Validation::required and Validation::upload, the checks do not check an empty value (they return true). Use required for required fields.$code decides the error message, see Configuration.

searchDocs.title: Methods​
searchDocs.content: 📄️Validation::__construct Create the validator and load the error messages 📄️Validation::required Check required 📄️Validation::alphameric Check half-width alphanumeric characters 📄️Validation::numeric Check numeric or not 📄️Validation::date Check date format 📄️Validation::email Check email address format 📄️Validation::tel Check telephone number format 📄️Validation::time Check time format 📄️Validation::url Check URL format 📄️Validation::zipcode Check Japanese postal code format 📄️Validation::userid Check user ID format 📄️Validation::password Check password format 📄️Validation::maxbyte Check maximum byte length 📄️Validation::length Check exact character length 📄️Validation::maxlength Check maximum character length 📄️Validation::minlength Check minimum character length 📄️Validation::hankaku Check half-width characters 📄️Validation::katakana Check Katakana characters for Japanese language 📄️Validation::upload Check that a file was uploaded 📄️Validation::setError Set an error by error code 📄️Validation::setErrorMessage Set an error message 📄️Validation::isError Check whether any error was set 📄️Validation::getErrorMessage Get error messages

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public boolean Validation::alphameric( string $name, mixed $value, [ mixed $code = '' ] )   Valid when the value contains only 0-9, a-z and A-Z.  An empty value ('', null, '0', whitespace only) is not checked and returns true: combine with Validation::required when the field is required. When $name already has an error, the check is skipped and returns false, so only the first error of each field is kept.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$name	string Field name (key of the error message) $value	mixed Value to check $code	mixed	''	Error code, array of error code and parameters, or error message (see Configuration)

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller use Fegg\Validation; $validation = new Validation(); $validation->alphameric('success', 'abc123', array('@alphameric', 'Code')); // -> true $validation->alphameric('failed', 'abc-123', array('@alphameric', 'Code')); // -> false var_dump($validation->getErrorMessage()); // -> array('failed' => '<strong>Code</strong> は半角英数で入力してください')

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public Validation::__construct( [ string $languageCode = '' ] )   Loads the error messages from validation_error_message.php (see Configuration). The file in site/config/ is used when it exists, otherwise the core's one.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$languageCode	string	''	Language code / if set, config/{languageCode}/validation_error_message.php is used (the file must exist)

searchDocs.title: Example​

searchDocs.title: Error messages​
searchDocs.content: The error messages are defined in htdocs/_fegg/core/config/validation_error_message.php.  To change them, do not edit the core: copy the file to htdocs/_fegg/site/config/validation_error_message.php and edit the copy. The file in site/config/ is used instead of the core's one (the whole file is replaced, so keep every key you use).  htdocs/_fegg/core/config/validation_error_message.php <?php defined('FEGG_CORE_DIR') || exit; /** * Error messages for the Validation class. * * @see Validation.php */ // @item should be Alphanumeric. $validation_error_message['@alphameric'] = '<strong>%s</strong> は半角英数で入力してください'; // @item is not Date format. $validation_error_message['@date'] = '<strong>%s</strong> の日付では登録できません'; // @item is not Email format. $validation_error_message['@email'] = '<strong>%s</strong> は登録できない形式です'; // @item should be half size character. $validation_error_message['@hankaku'] = '<strong>%s</strong> は半角で入力してください'; // @item should be KATAKANA. $validation_error_message['@katakana'] = '<strong>%s</strong> はカタカナで入力してください'; // @item must be at most N characters long. $validation_error_message['@maxlength'] = '<strong>%s</strong> は <strong>%s</strong> 文字以内で入力してください'; // @item must be at least N characters long. $validation_error_message['@minlength'] = '<strong>%s</strong> は <strong>%s</strong> 文字以上で入力してください'; // @item should be Numeric. $validation_error_message['@numeric'] = '<strong>%s</strong> は 半角数字で入力してください'; // @item should be Numeric to Integers or Decimals. $validation_error_message['@numeric_decimalpoint'] = '<strong>%s</strong> は 半角の整数もしくは小数で入力してください'; // @item should be half size character to Numeric and Minus sign. $validation_error_message['@numeric_minus'] = '<strong>%s</strong> は 数字、マイナス符号とも半角で入力してください'; // @item is unable character type. $validation_error_message['@password'] = '<strong>%s</strong> は登録できない形式です'; // @item should be mixing of alphanumeric. $validation_error_message['@password_mixed_letters'] = '<strong>%s</strong> は半角英数の混合で入力してください'; // @item is required. $validation_error_message['@required'] = '<strong>%s</strong> をご入力ください'; // @item is not Tel format. $validation_error_message['@tel'] = '<strong>%s</strong> は登録できない形式です'; // @item is not Time format. $validation_error_message['@time'] = '<strong>%s</strong> の時間では登録できません'; // @item is not Zipcode format. $validation_error_message['@zipcode'] = '<strong>%s</strong> は登録できない形式です';   There are no codes for url, userid, length and maxbyte. Pass the message itself, or add your own codes to the copy in site/config/.

searchDocs.title: The $code argument​
searchDocs.content: The $code argument of the check methods, Validation::setError and Validation::upload can be:  $code	Error message'@required'	The message of the code as it is array('@required', 'Name')	The message of the first element, with each %s replaced by the following elements in order (vsprintf()). An element that is itself a code (e.g. '@foo') is replaced by its message 'Please enter your name'	A string that is not a code is used as the message  Controller use Fegg\Validation; $validation = new Validation(); $validation->maxlength('name', $this->in('name'), 50, array('@maxlength', 'お名前', 50)); // -> '<strong>お名前</strong> は <strong>50</strong> 文字以内で入力してください' $validation->required('agree', $this->in('agree'), '<strong>利用規約</strong> に同意してください'); // -> '<strong>利用規約</strong> に同意してください'

searchDocs.title: Other languages​
searchDocs.content: When a language code is passed to the constructor (new Validation('en')), the messages are read from config/en/validation_error_message.php (searched in site/config/ first, then core/config/). The core has no language files: create the file in site/config/en/.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public boolean Validation::date( string $name, mixed $value, [ mixed $code = '' ] )   The separators / and - are removed, then the value must be digits only: YYYY (a year), YYYYMM (a year and a month from 01 to 12) or YYYYMMDD (an existing date, checked with checkdate()). So 2024, 2024/04, 2024-04-01 and 20240401 are valid; 2024/4/1 is not (8 digits are required for a day).  An empty value ('', null, '0', whitespace only) is not checked and returns true: combine with Validation::required when the field is required. When $name already has an error, the check is skipped and returns false, so only the first error of each field is kept.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$name	string Field name (key of the error message) $value	mixed Value to check $code	mixed	''	Error code, array of error code and parameters, or error message (see Configuration)

searchDocs.title: Example​

searchDocs.content: public boolean Validation::hankaku( string $name, mixed $value, [ mixed $code = '' ] )   Valid when the value contains no multi-byte character (the byte length equals the character length).  An empty value ('', null, '0', whitespace only) is not checked and returns true: combine with Validation::required when the field is required. searchDocs.title: Ticket​
searchDocs.content: Ticket is useful in securing your own form processing. Setting ticket will return a hashed random string using md5 function and is going to be a part of your session. This ticket can also be applied as Hidden input on the form. That means this ticket exists both on the server and client side and we can match them once the form is submitted and validate if they are the same.  📄️Application::setTicket Set ticket data and start ticket session 📄️Application::useTicket Use ticket once and destroy ticket session

searchDocs.title: What is a Controller?​
searchDocs.content: Controllers are the basis of the application, as it determines how requests are being handled in HTTP. A Controller is a class file that is named associated with a URI.  URL and Controller are closely related. (see URL)  http://exaple.com/foo/bar   In the example above, the framework will try to find a bar function in the controller named Foo.php and load it.  If the URL accessed from the given example, it would load in code/application/Foo.php given that this file exists.  code/application/Foo.php <?php class Foo extends Application { function bar(){ //process here... } }

searchDocs.title: Class​
searchDocs.content: You should have the same name class and file name, and extends Application class.  code/application/Controller.php <?php class Controller extends Application { }

searchDocs.title: Constructor​
searchDocs.content: You sould call parent(Application) class constructor.  code/application/Controller.php <?php class Controller extends Application { /** * Constructor */ function __construct() { parent::__construct(); } }

searchDocs.title: Initialize​
searchDocs.content: Fegg have a Initialize method apart from constructor.  It is __init() method that called after the constructor.  code/application/Controller.php <?php class Controller extends Application { /** * Initialize */ function __init() { // inityalize process } }   The difference between __init and constructor is that __init is run after make self instance, so it can use Application method by $this.  note You can omit a initialize.

searchDocs.title: Method​
searchDocs.content: Run a second segment name method in URL.  code/application/Controller.php <?php class Controller extends Application { // Run this function by http://example.com/controller/foo function foo() { // any process } }   If second segment is empty and you don’t edit basic settings, run the index() method.  code/application/Controller.php <?php class Controller extends Application { // Run this function by http://example.com/controller/index // or http://example.com/controller/ function index() { // any process } }   note See Initial settings about initial method name.  If you want to make a secret method, you should add underbar(_) head of method name.  code/application/Controller.php // http://example.com/controller/_secret // -> This URL don't call _secret() method <?php class Controller extends Application { // This method is secret from URL dispatcher function _secret() { // any process } }

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Third segment later are passed to a method.  code/application/Controller.php <?php class Controller extends Application { // $param will be assigned "bar" // by http://example.com/controller/foo/bar function foo( $param ) { echo $param; // bar } }   Third segment later are all passed.  code/application/Controller.php <?php class Controller extends Application { // $param1 will be "bar" and $param2 will be "baz" // by http://example.com/controller/foo/bar/baz function foo( $param1, $param2 ) { echo $param1; // bar echo $param2; // baz } }

searchDocs.title: Template of Controller class​
searchDocs.content: code/application/Index.php <?php /** * Index Class * // This file name should be Index.php */ class Index extends Application { /** * Constructor */ function __construct() { parent::__construct(); } /** * Initialize progress * This method run after making self instance. * So, it can use Application class method, for example "$this->in()". * It is the difference between __init and construct. * If this method is nothing, initializing progress is omitted. */ function __init() { } /** * Common progress * If you add the underbar(_) head of method name, it be internal method. * So, it can't called by URL dispatcher. */ function _common() { } /** * Default page display method * If you input only class name URL, run this method. * It is not necessary, but recommend be that default page display method name is index. */ function index() { // Common progress $this->_common(); // Display compiled template $this->displayPage('index'); } } /* End Of File: Index.php */

searchDocs.title: Arguments​

searchDocs.content: Controller $this->setTicket('foo'); $foo = $this->getSession('ticket_foo'); echo $foo;   Output 670f2f1232f30d4d716c1bc9c8a58388   Once the setTicket method is called, it will return a hashed random string and will start a new session with your given parameter as key prefixed with ticket_, the returned string will be its value. This will also automatically use the setHidden method that you can set on form for security evaluation.  Template {{ hidden }}   Output <input type='hidden' name='ticket_foo' value='670f2f1232f30d4d716c1bc9c8a58388' />

searchDocs.title: About Template​
searchDocs.content: Fegg is equipped with its own template engine where you can separate application code (PHP Code) and display (HTML/CSS). Fegg uses the {{}} tag for your application code in the template file. It runs a method that compile templates from Controller class.  Template files are save under the code/template/ directory with name format of template_name.tpl.

searchDocs.title: Display methods​
searchDocs.content: Display methods call the template file from Controller class.  Below are the display methods in Fegg but it is recommended to use only the displayPage method to avoid Clickjacking attacks.  📄️Application::displayTemplate Display compiled template 📄️Application::fetchTemplate Return compiled template into a string 📄️Application::fetchPage Return compiled template with declared controller and template variables into a string 📄️Application::displayPage Display compiled template with automatically variables and taking measures for Clickjacking

searchDocs.title: Template helper methods​
searchDocs.content: Template helper methods are used for passing special variable to the template.  📄️Application::setSiteinfo Set website information (ex. title, description, keywords) 📄️Application::setHidden Set hidden data 📄️Application::setHtmlHeader Set HTML Header

searchDocs.title: Template rules​
searchDocs.content: There are several operating notation for template file.  📄️Variable The use of variables in the template 📄️If if, else, else if 📄️Loop loop, foreach 📄️Include include, include head, head, include foot, foot 📄️Transclude transclude, section 📄️Checked/Selected checked, selected, options, hidden 📄️Options Make option tags 📄️Hidden Display hidden tag 📄️Code call, code

searchDocs.title: Modifiers​
searchDocs.content: You can modify the returned values of your variable in your application code in template using modifiers.  📄️Modifiers You can modify the returned values of your variable in your application code in template using modifiers.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public void Application::setHidden( mixed $name, [ string $value = "" ] )   Set input field hidden to your template from controller. In template, write {{ hidden }}, this will display <input type="hidden"> with your assigned name and value.  See also Hidden.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$id	string / array hidden name. If in array, syntax must be array($name => $value) $value	string	""	hidden value

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $this->setHidden( 'foo', 'bar' );   Template {{ hidden }}   Output <input type="hidden" name="foo" value="bar">

searchDocs.title: Assigning Multiple Parameters​
searchDocs.content: You can assign multiple parameters.  Controller $params = array( 'foo' => 'bar', 'baz' => 'qux', ); $this->setHidden($params);   Template {{ hidden }}   Output <input type="hidden" name="foo" value="bar"> <input type="hidden" name="baz" value="qux">

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public void Application::displayTemplate( string $template, [ array $assignedValue = array() ] )   Read template file -> compile -> display output.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$template	string Template file name $assignedValue	array	array()	Arguments for template

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: This reads the bar.tpl template file in code/template/foo/bar.tpl, compile it and display the compiled output.  code/application/Foo.php <?php class Foo extends Application { function bar(){ $this->displayTemplate( 'foo/bar' ); } }   note You should not include the “.tpl” extension in the parameter.  code/template/foo/bar.tpl <p>Variable : {{ $page.baz }}</p> <p>If else : {{ if true }}True{{ end }}</p> <p>Loop : {{ foreach $array as $k => $v }}{{ end foreach }}</p> <p>Template rule : {{ follow Fegg template rules }}</p>   Output Variable : If else : True Loop : Template rule : {{ follow Fegg template rules }}   Notice here the codes inside the {{}} in first 3 lines of paragraph in template file. In Fegg, these are the examples and valid syntax of application code following the Template rules, otherwise it will return as display or parse an error.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public string Application::fetchPage( string $template )   displayPage method is equipped with the X-Frame-Options HTTP response header set to Deny so that no other contents from the other sites are embedded into your website.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$template	string Template file name

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: code/application/Foo.php <?php class Foo extends Application { function bar(){ $this->displayPage( 'foo/bar' ); } }   Displays the Application::fetchPage result after taking precautionary measures from Clickjacking attack.  note It is recommended to use displayPage method in compiling your template file for the security of your web users/visitors.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public string Application::fetchTemplate( string $template, [ array $assignedValue = array() ] )   Returns the Application::displayTemplate into string without displaying the output.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$template	string Template file name $assignedValue	array	array()	Arguments for template

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: $content = $this->fetchTemplate( 'foo/bar' );   This assigned the Application::displayTemplate to $content variable from compiled template.  note You should not include the “.tpl” extension in the parameter.

searchDocs.title: How to use modifiers​
searchDocs.content: Modifiers are separated from the variable using pipe symbol ( | ) and may have an optional argument separated by colon symbol ( : ). Multiple modifiers can be chained, it modifies the variable from left to right. Thus, the output of the first filtering is applied to the next filtering.  {{ $var|noescape|function:param }}

searchDocs.title: noescape​
searchDocs.content: Fegg is automatically escaping character values. If you don’t want a escaping value, you can use the noescape modifier.  Controller $this->page['foo'] = '<p>bar</p>';   Template {{ $page.foo }} -> <p>bar</p> {{ $page.foo|noescape }} -> bar

searchDocs.title: br​
searchDocs.content: Insert HTML line breaks for all newline (\n) found in a string.  Controller $this->page['foo'] = "This is a test text.\n This is a new line text.";   Template {{ $page.foo }} -> This is a test text. This is a new line text. {{ $page.foo|br }} -> This is a test text. This is a new line text.

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: public string Application::fetchPage( string $template )   Returns the Application::displayTemplate result into string after including the assigned variables in controller class that can be use in template file.

searchDocs.title: Arguments​
searchDocs.content: Name	Data type	Default	Remarks$template	string Template file name

searchDocs.title: Appended arguments when compiling​
searchDocs.content: className Class name when running config Basic configuration languageCode Language code site Site parameters, assigned from Template helper (Application::setSiteinfo) page Assigned from Controller class in Requested parameters ($_POST / $_GET) hiddenForTemplate Input hidden parameters, assigned from Template helper (Application::setHidden) session Session data cookie Cookie data

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: code/application/Foo.php // URI: http://example.com/foo/bar/?get=param <?php class Foo extends Application { function bar(){ $this->page['baz'] = 'qux'; $content = $this->fetchPage( 'foo/bar' ); echo $content; } }   code/template/foo/bar.tpl Baz params : {{ $page.baz }} $_GET[get] params : {{ $in.get }} Controller name : {{ $classsName }}   Output Baz params : qux $_GET[get] params : param Controller name : foo   After assigning arguments for template, run the Application::fetchTemplate method.

searchDocs.title: code​
searchDocs.content: Template {{ code phpinfo(); }} // Run phpinfo();   Template {{ code $array = array('foo', 'bar'); var_dump( array_reverse($array) ); }} // Run $array = array('foo', 'bar'); var_dump( array_reverse($array) );   Output array(2) { [0]=> string(3) "bar" [1]=> string(3) "foo" }

searchDocs.title: call​
searchDocs.content: Template {{ call '/controller/method/params' }} // Call Controller::method('params'); {{ call '/Person/get/id/1' }} // Call Person::get('id', '1');

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $this->setHidden('foo', 'bar');   Template {{ hidden }}   Output <input type="hidden" name="foo" value="bar">

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: {{ checked key=$foo value=$bar }}   If value find in key, display checked="checked".  {{ selected key=$foo value=$bar }}   If value find in key, display selected="selected".

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Template /* $var = 'value'; $same = 'value'; $diff = 'not value'; */ <input type="checkbox" name="radio" value="{{ $same }}"{{ checked key=$same value=$var }}> {{ $same }} <input type="checkbox" name="radio" value="{{ $diff }}"{{ checked key=$diff value=$var }}> {{ $diff }} <select name="select"> <option value="{{ $same }}"{{ checked key=$same value=$var }}>{{ $same }}</option> <option value="{{ $diff }}"{{ checked key=$diff value=$var }}>{{ $diff }}</option> </select>   Output <input type="checkbox" name="radio" value="value" checked="checked"> value <input type="checkbox" name="radio" value="not value"> not value <select name="select"> <option value="value" selected="selected">value</option> <option value="not value">not value</option> </select>

searchDocs.title: Multiple checkbox​
searchDocs.content: /* $var = array('value1', 'value2'); $same1 = 'value1'; $same2 = 'value2'; $diff = 'not value'; */ <input type="checkbox" name="checkbox[]" value="{{ $same1 }}"{{ checked key=$same1 value=$var }}> {{ $same1 }} <input type="checkbox" name="checkbox[]" value="{{ $same2 }}"{{ checked key=$same2 value=$var }}> {{ $same2 }} <input type="checkbox" name="checkbox[]" value="{{ $diff }}"{{ checked key=$diff value=$var }}> {{ $diff }}   <input type="checkbox" name="checkbox[]" value="value1" checked="checked"> value <input type="checkbox" name="checkbox[]" value="value2" checked="checked"> value <input type="checkbox" name="checkbox[]" value="not value"> not value

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: {{ if }} {{ else if }} {{ else }} {{ end }}   It converted if section from {{ if }} to {{ end }}. You can use PHP comparison operators and methods in {{ if }} section, for example &&, ||, is_array, and so on.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Template {{ if $page.foo === 'bar' }} foo is bar {{ else if $page.foo === 'baz' }} foo is baz {{ else }} foo is neither bar nor baz {{ end }}

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Template /* $values = array( 'foo' => 'bar', 'baz' => 'qux' ); $selected = 'foo'; */ <select name="select"> {{ options source=$values selected=$selected }} </select>   Output <select name="select"> <option value="foo" selected="selected">bar</option> <option value="baz">qux</option> </select>

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: {{ loop $foo = $bar to $baz }} {{ end }}   {{ loop }} run looping until {{ end }} by assigned variables. It is same to for( $foo=$bar; $bar<=$baz; $foo++ ).  {{ foreach $array as $key => $val }} {{ end foreach }}   {{ foreach }} run looping until {{ end foreach }} by assigned array variable. You can get loop count from $foreachIndex in {{ foreach }}.

searchDocs.title: loop​
searchDocs.content: Template // $bar = 1, $baz = 5 <ul> {{ loop $foo = $bar to $baz }} <li>{{ $foo }}</li> {{ end }} </ul>   Output <ul> <li>1</li> <li>2</li> <li>3</li> <li>4</li> <li>5</li> </ul>

searchDocs.title: foreach​
searchDocs.content: Template // $array = array( 'foo' => 'bar', 'baz' => 'qux' ); <ul> {{ foreach $array as $key => $val }} <li>{{ $foreachIndex }} : {{ $key }} => {{ $val }}</li> {{ end foreach }} </ul>   Output <ul> <li>0 : foo => bar</li> <li>1 : bar => qux</li> </ul>

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: {{ include 'foo/bar' }}   {{ include head 'foo/bar' }} {{ head }}   {{ include foot 'foo/bar' }} {{ foot }}   Include another template.  {{ include }} read template and display writed place, but {{ include head }} and {{ include foot }} read template and display at {{ head }} and {{ foot }}.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Template - child.tpl <p>This file is child.tpl</p>   Template - parent.tpl <p>This file is parent.tpl</p> {{ include 'parts' }}   Output <p>This file is child.tpl</p> <p>This file is parent.tpl</p>   If use {{ include head }} and {{ include foot }}.  Template - header.tpl <link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="path/to/style.css">   Template - footer.tpl <script type="text/javascript" src="path/to/script.js"></script>   Template - parent.tpl {{ include head 'header' }} {{ include foot 'footer' }} <!DOCTYPE html> <html lang="en"> <head> <meta charset="UTF-8"> <title>Page title</title> {{ head }} </head> <body> something {{ foot }} </body> </html>   Output <!DOCTYPE html> <html lang="en"> <head> <meta charset="UTF-8"> <title>Page title</title> <link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="path/to/style.css"> </head> <body> something <script type="text/javascript" src="path/to/script.js"></script> </body> </html>

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: {{ $var }}   When display variables, you should write {{ $var }}. And when display array variables, you should separate period "." (ex: {{ $var.key }}).  If you want to give variable from Controller to template, you can assignment array value to $this->page, and then can display {{ $page.foo }} in Temaplte.  After compile, any variables display automatically through htmlSpecialChars method. If you want display raw variables, can display it use noescape modifire. Detail is see modifire.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Controller $this->page['foo'] = 'bar'; $this->displayPage( 'template' );   Template {{ $page.foo }}   Output bar

searchDocs.title: If you use noescape modifire.​
searchDocs.content: Controller $this->page['foo'] = '<p>bar</p>'; $this->displayPage( 'template' );   Template {{ $page.foo }} {{ $page.foo|noescape }}   Output &lt;p&gt;bar&lt;/p&gt; <p>bar</p>

searchDocs.title: Description​
searchDocs.content: {{ transclude 'foo/bar' }}   {{ section baz }} {{ end section baz }}   Transclude the other template. {{ transclude }} specify target template and display at {{ section }} area.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: Template - layout.tpl <!DOCTYPE html> <html lang="en"> <head> <meta charset="UTF-8"> <title>Page title</title> </head> <body> {{ section content }} {{ end section content }} </body> </html>   Template - index.tpl {{ transclude 'layout' }} {{ section content }} <p>This is a index content.</p> {{ end section content }}   Output <!DOCTYPE html> <html lang="en"> <head> <meta charset="UTF-8"> <title>Page title</title> </head> <body> <p>This is a index content.</p> </body> </html>

searchDocs.title: Mutiple transclude​
searchDocs.content: It can be mutiple transclude.  Template - grandparent.tpl <!DOCTYPE html> <html lang="en"> <head> <meta charset="UTF-8"> <title>Page title</title> </head> <body> <p>This is grandparent content.</p> {{ section content }} {{ end section content }} </body> </html>   Template - parent.tpl {{ transclude 'grandparent' }} {{ section content }} <div class="parent-box"> <p>This is parent content.</p> {{ section main }} {{ end section main }} </div> {{ end section content }}   Template - child.tpl {{ transclude 'parent' }} {{ section main }} <div class="child-box"> <p>This is child content.</p> </div> {{ end section main }}   Output <!DOCTYPE html> <html lang="en"> <head> <meta charset="UTF-8"> <title>Page title</title> </head> <body> <p>This is grandparent content.</p> <div class="parent-box"> <p>This is child content.</p> <div class="child-box"> <p>This is child content.</p> </div> </div> </body> </html>

searchDocs.title: Basic settings​
searchDocs.content: You can change the basic setting in fegg/settings.php.  Change the parameters of $settings in accordance to your environment.

searchDocs.title: Changing initial class and method name​
searchDocs.content: By default, initial class and method name is set to 'Index' file name and its 'index' method respectively. If you want to change the initial class and method name you should set your parameters in htdocs/index.php as seen below.  htdocs/index.php <?php // Default class name and method name if not set. if (!$fileName) { $fileName = 'Index'; } if (!$methodName) { $methodName = 'index'; }

searchDocs.title: URL and Controller class​
searchDocs.content: Fegg FW also adopted the segment-based-approach. Here is how the URL and Controller class relationship work.  http://example.com/class/function/param1/param2...   Class of ControllerMethod of Controller classArguments for Method  You can have a more flexible URL by setting up your URL structure in Routing file.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: URL http://example.com/post/edit/1   Running method <?php // code/application/Post.php class Post extends Application { // ... public function edit( $id ) { echo $id; // Result: 1 } // ... }

searchDocs.title: Routing​
searchDocs.content: You can set your URL structure without URL and Controller class relation by configuring your route file.  You may set your $route in array in code/config/route.php.  $route['from'] = 'to';   As described above, the Key of array is a segment of URL, whereas the Value of array is the value after remapping.  note Routes will run in order when they are defined. Higher routes will always take precedence over lower ones.

searchDocs.title: Wildcards​
searchDocs.content: There are 2 types of available wildcards (:any, :num) you may use before mapping key.  :any is any types of words. :num is limited only numbers.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: code/config/route.php <?php $route['foo'] = 'bar'; // http://example.com/foo -> code/application/Bar.php $route['item/:any'] = 'product/item_lookup/$1'; // http://example.com/item/foobar -> code/application/Product.php -> Product::item_lookup( 'foobar' ) $route['archive/edit/:num'] = 'post/edit/$1'; // http://example.com/archive/edit/1 -> code/application/Post.php -> Post::edit( 1 ) $route['news/post_:num.html'] = 'news/detail/$1'; // http://example.com/news/post_1.html -> code/application/News.php -> News::detail( 1 )

searchDocs.title: Fegg Directory structure
searchDocs.content: Fegg Directory structure Below is the initial folders and files you will see. Fegg consists of 3 main folders - code, fegg and htdocs. # The code folder organizes your application components. It has subfolders that contain your controller, template files, route, # cache and extension library. This folder is where you will work most of the time for the project development. code/ application/ ***.php # Controller classes config/ route.php # Set up a routing settings ***.php # Set up settings for other extension library data/ ... # Save cache file for Template engine and log file lib/ ***.php # Extension library classes template/ ***.tpl # Template files # The fegg folder is the Fegg core files. You don't need to edit these files. fegg/ Application.php # Fegg's Core file, include a basic class and functions settings.php # Set up basic settings for Fegg # The htdocs folder is where the document root is specified. htdocs/ .htaccess index.php # Dispatcher file In this user guide, it makes a description of the case, which were constructed in the above directory structure.

searchDocs.title: How to use​
searchDocs.content: You can load DB_pdo class through Application::getClass method.  Controller $database = $this->getClass('DB_pdo'); // Select query $result = $database->select('table_name')->execute()->all();

searchDocs.title: Methods​

searchDocs.title: Database connect setting​
searchDocs.content: You can change connect configuration on code/config/database_config.php.  database_config.php <?php /** * データベース接続先設定 * Database connect information * @see Database.php */ // 本番環境 // Production environment if (false) { // Database(Master)設定（１台を想定） // Database for Master $database_config['master'] = array( 'dsn' => 'sqlite:'.FEGG_CODE_DIR.'/data/db/db.db', 'username' => '', 'password' => '' ); // Database(Slave)設定（複数台を想定） // Database for Slave $database_config['slave'][] = array( 'dsn' => 'sqlite:'.FEGG_CODE_DIR.'/data/db/db.db', 'username' => '', 'password' => '' ); // 開発環境 // Development Environment } else { // Database(Master)設定（１台を想定） // Database for Master $database_config['master'] = array( 'dsn' => 'sqlite:'.FEGG_CODE_DIR.'/data/db/db.db', 'username' => '', 'password' => '' ); // Database(Slave)設定（複数台を想定） // Database for Slave $database_config['slave'][] = array( 'dsn' => 'sqlite:'.FEGG_CODE_DIR.'/data/db/db.db', 'username' => '', 'password' => '' ); } /* End of file database_config.php */

searchDocs.title: Automatic append query configuration​
searchDocs.content: You can arrange automatic append query configuration on code/config/database_regular_use_query.php.  database_regular_use_query.php <?php /** * 自動的付加クエリー * Automatic append query * @see Database.php * * DBクラスのselect, insert, update, deleteメソッド実行時に自動的付加するクエリー * （必要に応じて拡張していく予定） * * Automaticaly append query that "select", "insert", "update", "delete" method in DB Class. */ $database_regular_use_query = array( // テーブルに関わらず付加されるクエリー // Appended query regardless of table 'regular_use' => array( 'select' => array( 'where' => 'CURRENT_TABLE.valid = 1', 'order' => '', ), 'count' => array( 'where' => 'CURRENT_TABLE.valid = 1', 'order' => '', ), 'insert' => array( 'item' => 'modified = now(), created = now(), valid = 1', ), 'update' => array( 'item' => "modified = now()", 'where' => '', ), ), /* // テーブルに応じて付加されるクエリー // Appended query depending on table 'table' => array( 'table_name' => array( 'select' => array( 'where' => 'show_flag = 0', 'order' => '', ), 'insert' => array( 'item' => 'update_time = now(), create_datetime = now()', ), 'update' => array( 'item' => 'update_time = now()', 'where' => '', ), ), ), */ ); /* End of file database_regular_use_query.php */
